sentences.zh: 趙璜鄒文盛梁材劉麟蔣瑤王廷相

translations.literal: Zhao Huang, Zou Wencheng, Liang Cai, Liu Lin, Jiang Yao, Wang Tingxiang
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huang, Zou Wencheng, Liang Cai, Liu Lin, Jiang Yao, and Wang Tingxiang

sentences.zh: 喬宇，字希大，山西樂平人。

translations.literal: Qiao Yu, style name Xida, was a native of Leping in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Yu, whose style name was Xida, came from Leping in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 祖毅，工部左侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yi was Left Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yi had served as Left Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 父鳳，職方郎中。

translations.literal: His father Feng was a Director in the Bureau of Operations.
translations.idiomatic: His father Feng had been a director in the Bureau of Operations.

sentences.zh: 皆以清節顯。

translations.literal: Both were renowned for their integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Both were famed for their upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 宇登成化二十年進士，授禮部主事。

translations.literal: Yu passed the jinshi examination in the twentieth year of Chenghua and was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yu passed the jinshi examination in Chenghua 20 (1484) and received appointment as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，王恕為吏部，調之文選，三遷至郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi, when Wang Shu was Minister of Personnel, Yu was transferred to the Bureau of Appointments and was promoted three times to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongzhi reign, when Wang Shu headed the Ministry of Personnel, Yu was moved to the Bureau of Appointments and rose through three promotions to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 門無私謁。

translations.literal: No private callers came to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: He admitted no private callers at his gate.

sentences.zh: 擢太常少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 武宗嗣位，遣祀中鎮、西海。

translations.literal: When the Wuzong Emperor succeeded to the throne, Yu was sent to perform sacrifices at the Central Peak and the Western Sea.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wuzong Emperor came to the throne, Yu was dispatched to offer sacrifices at the Central Peak and the Western Sea.

sentences.zh: 還朝，條上道中所見軍民困苦六事。

translations.literal: On returning to court, he submitted in detail six matters of hardship among soldiers and civilians that he had observed along the road.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to court, he laid out in detail six hardships he had seen afflicting soldiers and civilians along the route.

sentences.zh: 已，遷光祿卿，歷戶部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was transferred to Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and served successively as Left and Right Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and then served in turn as Left and Right Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾敗，大臣多以黨附見劾，宇獨無所染。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin fell, many great ministers were impeached for factional attachment, but Yu alone was unstained.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin fell, many senior ministers were impeached for having joined his faction, but Yu alone remained untainted.

sentences.zh: 拜南京禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 乾清宮災，率同列言視朝不勤，經筵久輟，國本未建，義子猥多，番僧處禁寺，優伶侍起居，立皇店，留邊兵，習戰鬥，土木繁興，織造不息，凡十事。

translations.literal: When the Qianqing Palace burned, he led his colleagues in memorializing on ten matters: lax attendance at court audiences, the long suspension of the lecture series, the failure to establish the heir, the excessive number of adopted sons, Tibetan monks lodged in forbidden temples, actors attending the emperor's daily life, the establishment of imperial shops, the retention of frontier troops, training in combat, the profusion of construction projects, and the unceasing textile manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: After fire struck the Qianqing Palace, he led his colleagues in memorializing on ten abuses: neglect of court audiences, the long suspension of the lecture series, the failure to name an heir, the swarm of adopted sons, Tibetan monks quartered in forbidden temples, actors attending the emperor's private quarters, imperial shops, frontier troops kept on hand, drill in fighting, rampant construction, and unceasing textile manufacture.

sentences.zh: 帝不省。

translations.literal: The emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 久之，改兵部，參贊機務。

translations.literal: After a long while he was transferred to the Ministry of War and assisted in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was moved to the Ministry of War to assist in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 以帝遠遊塞上，而監國無人，請早建儲貳。

translations.literal: Because the emperor was touring far on the northern frontier while no one supervised the realm, he asked that the heir be established early.
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor was touring deep in the northern frontier while no one was left to supervise the realm, he urged that an heir be named without delay.

sentences.zh: 帝將自擊寇，宇復率同列諫。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to strike the enemy in person, Yu again led his colleagues in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor prepared to take the field against the enemy in person, Yu again led his colleagues in remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None received reply.
translations.idiomatic: None of these appeals received any reply.

sentences.zh: 未幾，寧王宸濠反，揚言旦夕下南京。

translations.literal: Before long the Prince of Ning, Chen Hao, rebelled and declared that he would descend on Nanjing within days.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Prince of Ning, Chen Hao, rose in rebellion and boasted that he would take Nanjing within days.

sentences.zh: 宇嚴為警備，而談笑自如。

translations.literal: Yu made strict preparations for defense yet conversed and laughed as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Yu put the defenses on a strict footing yet talked and laughed as calmly as ever.

sentences.zh: 時攜客燕城外，密察地險易，置戍守。

translations.literal: At times he took guests to feast outside the city wall, secretly surveying the terrain's advantages and difficulties and posting guards.
translations.idiomatic: At times he entertained guests outside the city walls, quietly surveying where the ground favored defense or attack and stationing guards accordingly.

sentences.zh: 綜理周密，內外宴然。

translations.literal: His overall arrangements were thorough, and within and without all was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: His arrangements were thorough inside and out, and the city remained calm.

sentences.zh: 指揮楊銳有才略，署為安慶守備。

translations.literal: The commander Yang Rui had talent and strategy; Yu appointed him to defend Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: The commander Yang Rui was capable and resourceful, and Yu put him in charge of the defense of Anqing.

sentences.zh: 鎮守中官劉郎與濠通，為預伏死士。

translations.literal: The eunuch commissioner Liu Lang was in communication with Hao and had secretly posted death squads.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch commissioner Liu Lang was in league with Hao and had secretly posted death squads in the city.

sentences.zh: 宇刺得其情，詰郎用事者，郎懼不敢動。

translations.literal: Yu probed and learned the facts, then questioned those who carried out Lang's orders; Lang was afraid and did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Yu investigated and uncovered the plot, then questioned the men carrying out Lang's orders; Lang was too frightened to move.

sentences.zh: 宇乃大索城中，斬所伏壯士三百人，懸首江上。

translations.literal: Yu then searched the city on a large scale, beheaded three hundred hidden strongmen, and hung their heads along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Yu then searched the city thoroughly, beheaded three hundred hidden strongmen, and hung their heads along the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 宸濠失內應，且知有備，不敢東。

translations.literal: Chen Hao lost his internal support and, knowing there were preparations, did not dare advance east.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao lost his inside support and, seeing that Nanjing was ready, did not dare march east.

sentences.zh: 攻安慶，銳固守不得下。

translations.literal: He attacked Anqing, but Yang Rui held firm and he could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Anqing, but Yang Rui held firm and the city would not fall.

sentences.zh: 未幾敗。

translations.literal: Before long he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was defeated.

sentences.zh: 帝至南京，詔百官戎服朝明年正旦。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached Nanjing, he ordered all officials to attend the New Year's audience of the coming year in military dress.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Nanjing, he ordered all officials to attend the coming New Year's audience in military dress.

sentences.zh: 宇不可，率諸臣朝服賀。

translations.literal: Yu would not agree and led the ministers in offering congratulations in court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Yu refused to comply and led the ministers in offering New Year's congratulations in court dress.

sentences.zh: 江彬索城門諸鑰，都督府問宇。

translations.literal: Jiang Bin demanded the keys to the city gates; the regional military commission asked Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bin demanded the keys to the city gates, and the regional military commission consulted Yu.

sentences.zh: 宇曰：「守備者，所以謹非常。

translations.literal: Yu said: "Defense preparations exist to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "Defenses exist to guard against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 禁門鎖鑰，孰敢索？

translations.literal: Who would dare demand the keys to the forbidden gates?
translations.idiomatic: Who would dare demand the keys to the forbidden gates?

sentences.zh: 亦孰敢予？

translations.literal: And who would dare hand them over?
translations.idiomatic: And who would dare hand them over?

sentences.zh: 雖天子詔不可得。」

translations.literal: Even an imperial edict from the Son of Heaven could not obtain them."
translations.idiomatic: Not even an edict from the Son of Heaven could obtain them."

sentences.zh: 都督府以宇言復，乃已。

translations.literal: The regional military commission reported Yu's words back, and the matter ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The regional military commission reported Yu's answer, and the demand was dropped.

sentences.zh: 彬矯旨有所求，日數十至，宇必廷白之，彬亦稍稍止。

translations.literal: Bin forged edicts to make demands that came dozens of times a day; Yu always stated them openly at court, and Bin gradually desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Bin forged edicts to press demands that arrived dozens of times a day; Yu always announced them openly at court, and Bin gradually backed off.

sentences.zh: 彬欲譖去宇。

translations.literal: Bin wished to slander Yu and have him removed.
translations.idiomatic: Bin wanted to slander Yu out of office.

sentences.zh: 守備太監王偉者，初為帝伴讀，帝信之，每從中調護，故彬謀不行。

translations.literal: The defense eunuch Wang Wei had originally been the emperor's study companion; the emperor trusted him, and he always mediated from within, so Bin's schemes did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The defense eunuch Wang Wei had once been the emperor's study companion; the emperor trusted him, and he always intervened from within, so Bin's plots came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 帝駐南京九月，宇倡諸臣三請回鑾，又自伏闕請。

translations.literal: The emperor stayed at Nanjing for nine months; Yu led the ministers in three requests to return to the capital and himself lay prostrate at the palace gate in petition.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lingered at Nanjing for nine months; Yu led the ministers in three appeals to return to the capital and himself lay prostrate at the palace gate in petition.

sentences.zh: 駕旋，扈至揚州。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage turned back, he escorted it as far as Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession turned homeward, he escorted it as far as Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年加太子太保。

translations.literal: The next year he was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 論保障功，復加少保。

translations.literal: In recognition of his merit in securing the realm, he was further made Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in securing the realm, he was further made Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，召為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor acceded, Yu was summoned as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizong Emperor came to the throne, Yu was summoned to serve as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 宇自為選郎，有人倫鑒，及是銓政一清。

translations.literal: Since his days as an appointments officer Yu had had a discerning eye for character, and now personnel administration was altogether purified.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since his days in the Bureau of Appointments Yu had shown a keen eye for character, and now personnel administration was altogether purified.

sentences.zh: 帝求治銳甚。

translations.literal: The emperor was very keen to seek good government.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was eager to set the realm in order.

sentences.zh: 宇與林俊、鼓澤、孫交，皆海內重望，帝亦委任之。

translations.literal: Yu, together with Lin Jun, Gu Ze, and Sun Jiao, all enjoyed great renown throughout the realm, and the emperor also entrusted them with authority.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, together with Lin Jun, Peng Ze, and Sun Jiao, all commanded great prestige throughout the realm, and the emperor entrusted them accordingly.

sentences.zh: 凡為權幸所黜者，皆起列庶位，天下欣欣望治。

translations.literal: All who had been dismissed by men in power were raised again to various posts, and the realm looked joyfully toward good government.
translations.idiomatic: All who had been ousted by the powerful were restored to office, and the realm looked on with hope for better days.

sentences.zh: 帝性剛，好自用，宇所執漸不見聽。

translations.literal: The emperor was by nature stubborn and fond of acting on his own judgment; Yu's views were gradually no longer heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was stubborn and inclined to have his own way; Yu's views were heard less and less.

sentences.zh: 興府需次官六十三人，乞遷敘。

translations.literal: Sixty-three officials of the Xing princedom awaiting promotion asked for advancement in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty-three officials of the Xing princedom who were awaiting promotion petitioned for advancement.

sentences.zh: 宇言此輩虛隸名籍，與見供事者不同。

translations.literal: Yu said that these men held empty places on the registers and differed from those actually serving in office.
translations.idiomatic: Yu argued that these men held nominal places on the registers and were not the same as officials actually serving in office.

sentences.zh: 黜罰之有差，皆怨宇。

translations.literal: Dismissals and penalties were meted out with distinctions, and all resented Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissals and penalties were applied in varying degrees, and all bore resentment against Yu.

sentences.zh: 帝欲封駙馬都尉崔元為侯，外戚蔣輪、邵喜為伯，宇不可。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to ennoble the Commandant-escort Cui Yuan as marquis and the maternal relatives Jiang Lun and Shao Xi as earls; Yu would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to ennoble the Commandant-escort Cui Yuan as marquis and the maternal relatives Jiang Lun and Shao Xi as earls, but Yu would not agree.

sentences.zh: 無何，詔進壽寧侯張鶴齡為公，封後父陳萬言為伯，授萬言子紹祖尚寶丞。

translations.literal: Before long an edict advanced Marquis Zhang Heling of Shouning to duke, ennobled the empress's father Chen Wanyan as earl, and appointed Wanyan's son Shaozu as Vice Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict advanced Marquis Zhang Heling of Shouning to duke, ennobled the empress's father Chen Wanyan as earl, and appointed Wanyan's son Shaozu Vice Director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 宇言：「累朝太后戚屬無生封公者，張巒亦歿後贈，今奈何以父贈為子封。

translations.literal: Yu said: "In successive reigns no maternal relative of an empress dowager was ennobled as duke during life; Zhang Luan too was posthumously honored only after death—how can a father's posthumous grant now become a son's living ennoblement?
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "In successive reigns no empress dowager's kin was ennobled as duke during life; Zhang Luan too was honored only after death—how can a father's posthumous grant now become a son's living ennoblement?

sentences.zh: 萬言封伯視巒更驟，而子授尚寶非制。

translations.literal: Wanyan's ennoblement as earl is even more abrupt than Luan's, and appointing his son to the Imperial Stud violates precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan's ennoblement as earl is even more abrupt than Luan's was, and appointing his son to the Imperial Stud violates precedent.

sentences.zh: 願陛下守典章，以垂萬世。」

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will uphold the statutes to bequeath them to ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty will uphold the statutes so they may endure for ages to come."

sentences.zh: 帝並不從。

translations.literal: The emperor would not follow any of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed any of it.

sentences.zh: 史道訐楊廷和，宇言道挾私，遂下之詔獄。

translations.literal: Shi Dao impeached Yang Tinghe; Yu said Dao was acting from private motives, and Dao was thereupon sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dao impeached Yang Tinghe; Yu said Dao was acting from private motives, and Dao was thereupon sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 曹嘉助道劾宇，宇求罷，帝命鴻臚趨視事。

translations.literal: Cao Jia aided Dao in impeaching Yu; Yu asked to resign, and the emperor ordered the Court of State Ceremonial to urge him to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jia aided Dao in impeaching Yu; Yu asked to resign, and the emperor ordered the Court of State Ceremonial to urge him back to duty.

sentences.zh: 宇遇事不可，無不力爭，而爭「大禮」尤切。

translations.literal: Whenever Yu found a matter unacceptable, he strove against it without fail, and his struggle over the "Great Rites" was especially fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yu found a matter unacceptable, he fought it without fail, and his opposition to the "Great Rites" controversy was especially fierce.

sentences.zh: 帝欲加興獻帝皇號，宇言加皇於本生之親，則幹正統，非所以重宗廟，正名分。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to add an imperial title to the Xing Sacrificial Emperor; Yu said that adding "emperor" to one's biological parent would disturb the legitimate succession and was not the way to honor the ancestral temple and rectify names and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to add an imperial title to his biological father, the Xing Sacrificial Emperor; Yu argued that calling one's biological parent "emperor" would disturb the legitimate succession and was not the way to honor the ancestral temple or keep names and ranks in order.

sentences.zh: 及禮官請稱獻帝為本生考，帝改稱本生皇考，又詔建獻帝廟於大內，宇等復連章諫。

translations.literal: When the ritual officials asked to style the Sacrificial Emperor as "biological father," the emperor changed this to "biological imperial father" and also ordered a temple to the Sacrificial Emperor built within the inner palace; Yu and others again submitted linked memorials in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When the ritual officials proposed styling the Sacrificial Emperor as "biological father," the emperor changed this to "biological imperial father" and also ordered a temple to him built within the inner palace; Yu and others again submitted linked memorials in remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 特旨用席書為禮部尚書，宇又偕九卿言：「陛下罷汪俊，用席書；

translations.literal: By special edict Xi Shu was appointed Minister of Rites; Yu again joined the Nine Ministers in saying: "Your Majesty dismissed Wang Jun and employed Xi Shu;
translations.idiomatic: By special edict Xi Shu was appointed Minister of Rites; Yu again joined the Nine Ministers in saying, "Your Majesty dismissed Wang Jun and employed Xi Shu;

sentences.zh: 謫馬明衡、季本、陳逅，召張璁、桂萼、霍韜。

translations.literal: demoted Ma Mingheng, Ji Ben, and Chen Hou, and summoned Zhang Cong, Gui E, and Huo Tao.
translations.idiomatic: demoted Ma Mingheng, Ji Ben, and Chen Hou, and summoned Zhang Cong, Gui E, and Huo Tao.

sentences.zh: 舉措乖違，人心駭愕。

translations.literal: These measures were contrary to propriety and struck the hearts of men with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: These measures violated propriety and filled men's hearts with alarm.

sentences.zh: 夫以一二人邪說，廢天下萬世公議，內離骨肉，外間君臣，名為效忠，實累聖德。

translations.literal: To discard the public consensus of the realm for ten thousand generations on account of the heterodox talk of one or two men, to estrange kin within and set ruler and minister at odds without, to call it loyalty while in truth burdening sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: To set aside the consensus of the realm for all time on account of the heterodox views of one or two men, to estrange kin within and set ruler and minister at odds without, to call it loyalty while in truth burdening Your Majesty's virtue.

sentences.zh: 且書不繇廷推，特出內降，此祖宗來所未有。

translations.literal: Moreover, Shu was not chosen through court recommendation but issued by a special inner edict—something unprecedented since the founding ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Shu was not chosen through court recommendation but appointed by a special inner edict—something unprecedented since the founding ancestors.

sentences.zh: 乞令俊與書各仍舊職，宥明衡等，止璁、萼毋召。」

translations.literal: We beg that Jun and Shu each return to their former posts, that Mingheng and the others be pardoned, and that Cong and E not be summoned."
translations.idiomatic: We beg that Jun and Shu each return to their former posts, that Mingheng and the others be pardoned, and that Cong and E not be summoned."

sentences.zh: 尋復請罷璁、萼、書，而出爭「大禮」者呂柟、鄒守益於獄。

translations.literal: Soon they again asked that Cong, E, and Shu be dismissed, while those who had contested the "Great Rites," Lü Zan and Zou Shouyi, were released from prison.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they again asked that Cong, E, and Shu be dismissed, while Lü Zan and Zou Shouyi, who had contested the "Great Rites," were released from prison.

sentences.zh: 會璁、萼至京，詔皆用為學士。

translations.literal: When Cong and E reached the capital, an edict appointed both as Hanlin Academicians.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong and E reached the capital, an edict appointed both Hanlin Academicians.

sentences.zh: 宇等又言：「內降恩澤，先朝率施於佞幸小人。

translations.literal: Yu and others again said: "Favors granted by inner edict were in former reigns generally bestowed on fawning favorites and petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and others again said, "Favors granted by inner edict were in former reigns generally bestowed on fawning favorites and petty men.

sentences.zh: 若士大夫一預其間，即不為清議所齒。

translations.literal: If a scholar-official should share in such favor even once, he would no longer be accepted by pure opinion.
translations.idiomatic: If a scholar-official should share in such favor even once, respectable opinion would no longer accept him.

sentences.zh: 況學士最清華，而俾萼等居之，誰復肯與同列哉？」

translations.literal: Moreover, the Hanlin Academician is the most exalted and pure of posts—if men like E are placed in it, who would still be willing to serve in the same ranks?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Hanlin Academician is the most exalted and pure of posts—if men like E are placed in it, who would still be willing to serve alongside them?"

sentences.zh: 帝怒，切責。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and sharply rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and sharply rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 宇遂乞休，許之。

translations.literal: Yu then asked to retire, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yu then asked to retire, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 馳傳給夫廩，猶如故事。

translations.literal: Relay horses, bearers, and stipends were provided as of old custom.
translations.idiomatic: Relay horses, bearers, and stipends were provided according to established custom.

sentences.zh: 御史許中、劉隅等請留宇，帝曰：「朕非不用宇，宇自以疾求去耳。」

translations.literal: The censors Xu Zhong, Liu Yu, and others asked that Yu be retained; the emperor said: "It is not that I will not use Yu—Yu himself asked to leave on grounds of illness."
translations.idiomatic: The censors Xu Zhong, Liu Yu, and others asked that Yu be retained; the emperor said, "It is not that I refuse to use Yu—Yu himself asked to leave on grounds of illness."

sentences.zh: 後《明倫大典》成，追論前議，奪官。

translations.literal: Later, when the 《Minglun Dadian》 (Comprehensive Canon of Human Relations) was completed, earlier opinions were reviewed retrospectively and his office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the 《Minglun Dadian》 (Comprehensive Canon of Human Relations) was completed, earlier opinions were reviewed retrospectively and his office was stripped.

sentences.zh: 楊一清卒，宇渡江吊之。

translations.literal: When Yang Yiqing died, Yu crossed the river to offer mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yiqing died, Yu crossed the river to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 南都父老皆出迎，舉手加額曰：「活我者，公也。」

translations.literal: The elders of the southern capital all came out to welcome him, raising their hands to their foreheads and saying: "The one who saved our lives was you, sir."
translations.idiomatic: The elders of the southern capital all came out to welcome him, raising their hands to their foreheads and saying, "You, sir, are the one who saved our lives."

sentences.zh: 宇幼從父京師，學於楊一清。

translations.literal: In youth Yu followed his father to the capital and studied under Yang Yiqing.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Yu followed his father to the capital and studied under Yang Yiqing.

sentences.zh: 成進士後，復從李東陽遊。

translations.literal: After becoming a jinshi, he again associated with Li Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he again associated with Li Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 詩文雄雋，兼通篆籀。

translations.literal: His poetry and prose were bold and keen, and he was also versed in seal and ancient scripts.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose were bold and accomplished, and he was also versed in seal and ancient scripts.

sentences.zh: 性好山水，嘗陟太華絕頂。

translations.literal: By nature he loved mountains and rivers and once climbed to the summit of Mount Taihua.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved mountains and rivers and once climbed to the summit of Mount Taihua.

sentences.zh: 遇虎，仆夫皆驚仆，宇端坐不動，虎徐帖尾去。

translations.literal: He met a tiger; all the servants fell down in fright, but Yu sat upright without moving, and the tiger slowly lowered its tail and went away.
translations.idiomatic: He met a tiger; all the servants fell down in fright, but Yu sat upright without moving, and the tiger slowly lowered its tail and walked away.

sentences.zh: 家居淡泊，服禦若寒士。

translations.literal: At home he lived plainly, his clothing and equipage like those of a poor scholar.
translations.idiomatic: At home he lived plainly, his clothing and equipage like those of a poor scholar.

sentences.zh: 身歿，二妾劉、許皆從死。

translations.literal: When he died, his two concubines Liu and Xu both followed him in death.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, his two concubines, Liu and Xu, both took their own lives to follow him.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，復官，贈少傅，謚莊簡。

translations.literal: When the Muzong Emperor ascended the throne, his offices were restored; he was posthumously given Junior Grand Mentor and granted the posthumous name Zhuangjian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Muzong Emperor came to the throne, Yu's offices were restored; he was posthumously made Junior Grand Mentor and given the posthumous name Zhuangjian.

sentences.zh: 孫交，字誌同，陸安人。

translations.literal: Sun Jiao, courtesy name Zhitong, was a native of Lu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jiao, courtesy name Zhitong, was a native of Lu'an.

sentences.zh: 成化十七年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the seventeenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventeenth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 授南京兵部主事，為尚書王恕所知。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of War and was recognized by Minister Wang Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of War and came to the attention of Minister Wang Shu.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，怒入吏部，薦授稽勛員外郎，歷文選郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi, when Wang Shu entered the Ministry of Personnel, [Jiao] was recommended and appointed Vice Director in the Office of Merit Records, and served successively as Director in the Office of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Hongzhi reign, when Wang Shu took office at the Ministry of Personnel, Jiao was recommended and appointed Vice Director in the Office of Merit Records, then served as Director in the Office of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 居吏部十四年，於善類多所推引。

translations.literal: He remained at the Ministry of Personnel for fourteen years and recommended many worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: He served at the Ministry of Personnel for fourteen years and recommended many worthy men to office.

sentences.zh: 遷太常少卿，提督四夷館。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Ceremonies and placed in charge of the Bureau of the Four Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Ceremonies and put in charge of the Bureau of the Four Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 大同有警，命經略黃花鎮諸邊。

translations.literal: When Datong was threatened, he was ordered to oversee the borders around Huanghua Fort.
translations.idiomatic: When Datong came under threat, he was ordered to take charge of the frontier defenses around Huanghua Fort.

sentences.zh: 增垣塹，廣樹藝，制敵騎馳突。

translations.literal: He raised walls and ditches, widely planted crops, and checked enemy cavalry charges.
translations.idiomatic: He raised walls and ditches, expanded cultivation, and checked enemy cavalry raids.

sentences.zh: 永樂時，歲遣隆慶諸衛軍采薪炭。

translations.literal: In the Yongle era, each year troops from the Longqing garrisons were dispatched to gather firewood and charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongle era, each year troops from the Longqing garrisons were sent to gather firewood and charcoal.

sentences.zh: 其後罷之，令歲輸銀二萬兩，軍重困。

translations.literal: Later this was abolished and they were required to pay twenty thousand taels of silver annually; the troops were heavily burdened.
translations.idiomatic: Later the practice was abolished and the troops were instead required to pay twenty thousand taels of silver each year, leaving them heavily burdened.

sentences.zh: 交奏免之。

translations.literal: Jiao memorialized to have it abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao memorialized asking that the levy be abolished.

sentences.zh: 正德初，擢光祿卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde, he was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhengde reign, he was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 三年進戶部右侍郎，提督倉場，改吏部。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue, placed in charge of the granaries, and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Right Vice Minister of Revenue and put in charge of the granaries, then transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 尚書張彩附劉瑾，交數規切。

translations.literal: Minister Zhang Cai was allied with Liu Jin; Jiao repeatedly admonished him sharply.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhang Cai was allied with Liu Jin, and Jiao repeatedly remonstrated with him in sharp terms.

sentences.zh: 彩怒，調之南京。

translations.literal: Cai was angered and transferred him to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Cai was enraged and had him transferred to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 瑾敗，召拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When Jin fell, [Jiao] was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin fell, Jiao was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時征討流寇，調度煩急，仍歲兇，正賦不足，交區畫適宜。

translations.literal: At the time campaigns against roving bandits made dispatch urgent; famine struck year after year and regular taxes were insufficient; Jiao planned allocations appropriately.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the state was campaigning against roving bandits and dispatch was urgently pressed; famine followed famine and regular revenues fell short, yet Jiao arranged finances appropriately.

sentences.zh: 四方告饑，輒請蠲租遣振，以故民不至甚敝，而小人用事者皆不便之。

translations.literal: When famine was reported from all quarters, he repeatedly petitioned to remit taxes and dispatch relief, so the people did not become utterly destitute, yet the petty men in power all found this inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever famine was reported from the provinces, he repeatedly asked to remit taxes and send relief, so the people did not become utterly ruined; yet the petty men then in power all found this inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 帝欲以太平倉賜幸臣裴德，雲南鎮守中官張倫請采銀礦，南京織造中官吳經奏費乏，交皆力爭。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to grant the Taiping Granary to the favored minister Pei De; the eunuch supervisor at Yunnan Zhang Lun requested to mine silver; the Nanjing weaving eunuch Wu Jing memorialized that funds were lacking; Jiao strenuously opposed all of these.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to grant the Taiping Granary to his favorite Pei De; the Yunnan garrison eunuch Zhang Lun asked to open silver mines; the Nanjing weaving eunuch Wu Jing reported that funds were exhausted—and Jiao fought every proposal.

sentences.zh: 八年六月，中旨與禮部尚書傅珪並致仕。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eighth year, by direct imperial order he and Minister of Rites Fu Gui were both made to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the eighth year, by direct imperial order he and Minister of Rites Fu Gui were both forced to retire.

sentences.zh: 言官多請留，不報。

translations.literal: Many censors asked that he be retained; no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: Many censorial officials asked that he be kept in office, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 世宗在潛邸知交名，甫即位，召復故官。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor knew Jiao's reputation while still heir apparent; as soon as he ascended the throne, he summoned Jiao back to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizong Emperor had known Jiao's reputation while still heir apparent; as soon as he took the throne, he recalled Jiao to his former post.

sentences.zh: 首請帝日讀《祖訓》，言動悉取準則，經筵日講寒暑勿輟。

translations.literal: He first asked the emperor to read the Ancestral Instructions daily, take them as the standard for word and deed, and never skip the daily lecture—winter or summer.
translations.idiomatic: He first asked the emperor to read the Ancestral Instructions every day, take them as the standard for word and deed, and never miss the daily lecture, whether in heat or cold.

sentences.zh: 帝褒納焉。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the advice and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 或議遷顯陵天壽山，交言：「山陵事重，太祖欲遷仁祖於鐘山，慮泄靈氣而止，具載《皇陵碑》。」

translations.literal: Some proposed moving the Xianling mausoleum to Tianshou Mountain; Jiao said: "Matters of mountain tombs are weighty. The Taizu Emperor wished to move Renzu to Mount Zhong but stopped for fear of draining spiritual potency; this is fully recorded in the Imperial Mausoleum Stele."
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed moving the Xianling mausoleum to Tianshou Mountain; Jiao said, "Matters of imperial tombs are grave. The Taizu Emperor wished to move Renzu to Mount Zhong but stopped for fear of draining its spiritual potency—this is fully recorded in the Imperial Mausoleum Stele."

sentences.zh: 事乃止。

translations.literal: The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was then dropped.

sentences.zh: 武宗侈汰之後，庫藏殫虛。

translations.literal: After the Wuzong Emperor's extravagance, the treasury was utterly emptied.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wuzong Emperor's extravagance, the treasury was utterly depleted.

sentences.zh: 交裁冗食，定經制，宿弊為清。

translations.literal: Jiao cut redundant stipends, fixed permanent regulations, and longstanding abuses were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao cut redundant stipends, set fixed regulations, and cleared away longstanding abuses.

sentences.zh: 然事涉中官者，帝亦不能盡從也。

translations.literal: Yet on matters involving eunuchs, the emperor could not fully follow [Jiao's advice].
translations.idiomatic: Yet on matters involving eunuchs, the emperor could not fully follow his advice.

sentences.zh: 嘗會廷臣議發內帑給軍廩官俸，已報可，為中官梁諫等所沮。

translations.literal: Once he convened court officials to discuss disbursing from the inner treasury for military rations and official salaries; approval was already given, but it was blocked by the eunuchs Liang Jian and others.
translations.idiomatic: Once he convened the court to discuss drawing from the inner treasury for military rations and official salaries; approval had already been given, but the eunuchs Liang Jian and others blocked it.

sentences.zh: 交言：「宮府異同，令出復反，非新政所宜。」

translations.literal: Jiao said: "When palace and government differ and orders issue then reverse, this is not fitting for the new reign."
translations.idiomatic: Jiao said, "When palace and government disagree and orders are issued only to be reversed, this is not fitting for a new reign."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: [The emperor] did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 中官監督倉場者，初止數人，正德中增至五十五人。

translations.literal: Eunuchs supervising granaries had initially numbered only a few; in Zhengde they increased to fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs supervising granaries had initially numbered only a few, but in the Zhengde reign they increased to fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 以交言罷撤過半，其後復漸增。

translations.literal: On Jiao's advice more than half were dismissed, but numbers gradually increased again thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: On Jiao's advice more than half were dismissed, but their numbers gradually rose again afterward.

sentences.zh: 帝已罷三十七人，交欲盡去之，並臨清、徐、淮諸倉，一切勿遣。

translations.literal: The emperor had already dismissed thirty-seven; Jiao wished to remove them all entirely, including at the Linqing, Xuzhou, and Huai granaries—none to be dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already dismissed thirty-seven of them, but Jiao wanted them all removed, including at the Linqing, Xuzhou, and Huai granaries—none to be sent at all.

sentences.zh: 帝令自今毋更加而已。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered only that no more be added from then on.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered only that no more be added from then on.

sentences.zh: 守珠池中官，詔毋得預守土事，而安川夤緣復故。

translations.literal: Regarding eunuchs guarding the pearl pool, an edict forbade them from interfering in local administration, but An Chuan used connections to resume his old ways.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had forbidden eunuchs guarding the pearl pool from interfering in local administration, but An Chuan used connections to resume his old conduct.

sentences.zh: 交劾川，命如前詔。

translations.literal: Jiao impeached Chuan; the order was as in the previous edict.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao impeached An Chuan, and the emperor ordered matters handled as in the earlier edict.

sentences.zh: 正德中，上林苑內臣至九十九人，侵奪公私地無算。

translations.literal: In Zhengde, inner attendants of the Imperial Park reached ninety-nine and seized countless tracts of public and private land.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengde reign, inner attendants of the Imperial Park reached ninety-nine in number and seized untold tracts of public and private land.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，命留十八人，如弘治時。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, he ordered that eighteen be retained, as in the Hongzhi era.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, he ordered that eighteen be kept, as in the Hongzhi era.

sentences.zh: 已復傳奉至六十二人，交乞汰如初，且盡歸侵奪地。

translations.literal: Soon special appointments again reached sixty-two; Jiao asked that they be reduced as at first and that all seized land be fully returned.
translations.idiomatic: Before long specially appointed eunuchs again reached sixty-two; Jiao asked that they be reduced as at first and that all seized land be fully returned.

sentences.zh: 報許。

translations.literal: Permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 又論禦馬監內臣宜如祖制，毋監收芻豆，並令戶部通知馬數，杜其侵耗。

translations.literal: He also argued that eunuchs of the Imperial Stud should follow ancestral institutions, not supervise the collection of fodder and beans, and that the Ministry of Revenue should be notified of horse counts to stop their embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that eunuchs of the Imperial Stud should follow ancestral practice, not supervise the collection of fodder and beans, and that the Ministry of Revenue should be notified of horse numbers to stop their embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: [The emperor] did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not comply.

sentences.zh: 錦衣百戶張瑾率校尉支俸通倉，橫取狼藉，主事羅洪載欲按之。

translations.literal: Jinyi Regiment hundred-household Zhang Jin led bailiffs to draw salaries from the Tong Granary and seized goods wantonly; Secretary Luo Hongzai wished to investigate him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin, a hundred-household of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, led bailiffs to draw pay from the Tong Granary and seized goods with reckless abandon; Secretary Luo Hongzai wanted to investigate him.

sentences.zh: 瑾紿請受杖，奏洪載擅笞禁衛官。

translations.literal: Jin deceptively asked to accept beating, then memorialized that Hongzai had unlawfully flogged an imperial guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: Jin tricked him by asking to accept a beating, then memorialized that Hongzai had unlawfully flogged an imperial guard officer.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，逮下詔獄謫外。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged; [Hongzai] was arrested, sent to the imperial prison, and demoted abroad.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged; Hongzai was arrested, sent to the imperial prison, and demoted to service outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 交與林俊、喬宇先後論救，不納。

translations.literal: Jiao, Lin Jun, and Qiao Yu successively memorialized in his defense; [the emperor] did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao, Lin Jun, and Qiao Yu successively memorialized in his defense, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 禦馬監閻洪乞外豹房地，交言：「先帝以豹房故，貽禍無窮。

translations.literal: Eunuch of the Imperial Stud Yan Hong requested outer leopard-house lands; Jiao said: "The previous emperor, because of the leopard quarters, bequeathed endless calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Hong of the Imperial Stud asked for outer leopard-house lands; Jiao said, "The previous emperor, because of the leopard quarters, bequeathed endless calamity.

sentences.zh: 洪等欲修復以開遊獵之端，非臣等所敢聞。」

translations.literal: Hong and others wish to restore them and open the door to hunting excursions—this is not something we ministers dare hear of."
translations.idiomatic: Hong and the others wish to restore them and reopen the door to hunting excursions—this is not something we ministers dare even hear proposed."

sentences.zh: 詔以地十頃給豹房，余令百戶趙愷等佃如故。

translations.literal: An edict granted ten qing of land to the leopard quarters; the rest was ordered leased as before by hundred-household Zhao Kai and others.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted ten qing of land to the leopard quarters; the rest was ordered leased as before by Zhao Kai and other hundred-households.

sentences.zh: 奉詔上各宮莊田數，視舊籍不同，帝詰其故。

translations.literal: As ordered he submitted the acreages of each palace estate; they differed from the old register, and the emperor demanded the reason.
translations.idiomatic: As ordered he submitted the acreages of each palace estate; they differed from the old register, and the emperor demanded an explanation.

sentences.zh: 交言：「舊籍多以奏請投獻，數多妄報也。

translations.literal: Jiao said: "The old register mostly reflected petitions and offerings of land; the figures were often falsely reported.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao said, "The old register mostly reflected lands offered through petitions and gifts; the figures were often falsely inflated.

sentences.zh: 新籍少，以奉命清核，田多除豁也。」

translations.literal: The new register is smaller because, on order, a thorough audit cleared and exempted much land."
translations.idiomatic: The new register is smaller because, on imperial order, a thorough audit cleared and exempted much land."

sentences.zh: 帝意稍解，令考成、弘間籍以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor's mood eased somewhat and he ordered registers from the Chenghua and Hongzhi reigns examined and reported.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger eased somewhat, and he ordered registers from the Chenghua and Hongzhi reigns examined and reported.

sentences.zh: 交年已七十，連章乞罷。

translations.literal: Jiao was already seventy and repeatedly memorialized to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao was already seventy and repeatedly memorialized asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝輒慰留，遣醫視療。

translations.literal: The emperor always comforted him and kept him on, sending physicians to treat him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor always comforted him and kept him in office, sending physicians to treat him.

sentences.zh: 請益力，乃許之。

translations.literal: When his petitions grew more forceful, permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When his petitions grew more insistent, permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 手詔加太子太保，馳驛。

translations.literal: By handwritten edict he was given the added title Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and granted relay horses.
translations.idiomatic: By handwritten edict he was given the added title Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and granted relay horses for his journey home.

sentences.zh: 令子編修元侍行，有司時存問，給食米輿隸，復賜道里費。

translations.literal: He ordered his son, Hanlin compiler Yuan, to accompany him; local offices were to inquire after him regularly, provide grain, rice, sedan bearers, and attendants, and he was again granted travel expenses.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his son Yuan, a Hanlin compiler, to accompany him; local offices were to inquire after him regularly and provide grain, rice, sedan bearers, and attendants, and he was again granted travel expenses.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十，謚榮僖。

translations.literal: He died at eighty and was granted the posthumous name Rongxi.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty and was given the posthumous name Rongxi.

sentences.zh: 交言論恂恂，不以勢位驕人。

translations.literal: Jiao was gentle and respectful in speech and did not act arrogantly toward others because of rank and power.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao was gentle and respectful in speech and did not lord his rank and power over others.

sentences.zh: 清慎恬愨，終始一致。

translations.literal: Pure, cautious, tranquil, and sincere—consistent from first to last.
translations.idiomatic: Pure, cautious, tranquil, and sincere, he was the same from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 初在南京，僚友以事簡多暇，相率談諧飲弈為樂，交默處一室，讀書不輟。

translations.literal: When first in Nanjing, colleagues, finding their duties light with much leisure, together made merry with conversation, drink, and chess; Jiao quietly remained in one room, reading without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first in Nanjing, his colleagues, finding their duties light and themselves with much leisure, would together amuse themselves with talk, drink, and chess; Jiao quietly stayed in one room and read without stopping.

sentences.zh: 或以為言，交曰：「對聖賢語，不愈於賓客、妻妾乎！」

translations.literal: When some commented on this, Jiao said: "Speaking with sages—is that not better than guests or wives and concubines!"
translations.idiomatic: When some remarked on this, Jiao said, "Is speaking with the sages not better than speaking with guests, or wives and concubines!"

sentences.zh: 興獻王素愛重交，嘗割陽春臺東偏地益其宅。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xingxian had always esteemed Jiao and once ceded land east of Yangchun Terrace to enlarge his residence.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xingxian had always held Jiao in high regard and once ceded land east of Yangchun Terrace to enlarge his residence.

sentences.zh: 後中官言孫尚書侵地，世宗曰：「此先皇所賜，吾敢奪耶？」

translations.literal: Later a eunuch said Minister Sun had encroached on land; the Shizong Emperor said: "This was granted by the late emperor—how dare I take it away?"
translations.idiomatic: Later a eunuch said that Minister Sun had encroached on land, and the Shizong Emperor said, "This was granted by the late emperor—how dare I seize it?"

sentences.zh: 元，進士，終四川副使。

translations.literal: Yuan became a jinshi and ended as Vice Commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan passed the jinshi examination and ended his career as Vice Commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 謹厚有父風。

translations.literal: Careful and solid, he had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Careful and solid, he had his father's character.

sentences.zh: 林俊，字待用，莆田人。

translations.literal: Lin Jun, courtesy name Daiyong, was a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Jun, courtesy name Daiyong, was a native of Putian.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fourteenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 除刑部主事，進員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice and promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice and promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 性侃直，不隨俗浮湛。

translations.literal: By nature he was outspoken and upright and did not drift with the tide.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was outspoken and upright and did not drift with the crowd.

sentences.zh: 事涉權貴，尚書林聰輒屬俊治之。

translations.literal: When cases involved powerful figures, Minister Lin Cong always assigned Jun to handle them.
translations.idiomatic: When cases involved the powerful, Minister Lin Cong always assigned Jun to handle them.

sentences.zh: 上疏請斬妖僧繼曉並罪中貴梁芳，帝大怒，下詔獄考訊。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting execution of the heterodox monk Jixiao and punishment of the favored eunuch Liang Fang; the emperor was greatly angered and had him sent to the imperial prison for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking that the heterodox monk Jixiao be executed and the favored eunuch Liang Fang punished; the emperor was greatly angered and had him sent to the imperial prison for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 後府經歷張黻救之，並下獄。

translations.literal: Chief clerk Zhang Fu of the Rear Palace came to his defense and was also imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu, a chief clerk of the Rear Palace, came to his defense and was imprisoned as well.

sentences.zh: 太監懷恩力救，俊得謫姚州判官，黻師宗知州。

translations.literal: Eunuch Huai'en rescued them strenuously; Jun was demoted to magistrate of Yaozhou, Fu to prefect of Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Huai'en intervened forcefully on their behalf; Jun was demoted to magistrate of Yaozhou, and Fu to prefect of Shizong.

sentences.zh: 時言路久塞，兩人直聲震都下，為之語曰：「御史在刑曹，黃門出後府。」

translations.literal: At the time the channels of remonstrance had long been blocked; the upright reputations of the two men shook the capital, and people said of them: "The censor is in the Ministry of Justice; the gate officer came from the Rear Palace."
translations.idiomatic: At the time the channels of remonstrance had long been blocked; the two men's reputations for integrity shook the capital, and people said of them, "The censor is in the Ministry of Justice; the gate officer came from the Rear Palace."

sentences.zh: 尋以正月朔星變，帝感悟，復俊官，改南京。

translations.literal: Soon, on the first day of the first month, there was a stellar anomaly; the emperor was moved and restored Jun's office, transferring him to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, on the first day of the first month, a stellar anomaly occurred; the emperor was moved and restored Jun to office, transferring him to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年用薦擢雲南副使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongzhi he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of Yunnan on recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongzhi he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of Yunnan on recommendation.

sentences.zh: 鶴慶玄化寺稱有活佛，歲時集士女萬人，爭以金塗其面。

translations.literal: At Xuanhua Temple in Heqing there was said to be a living buddha; each year tens of thousands of men and women gathered, competing to gild its face with gold.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuanhua Temple in Heqing there was said to be a living buddha; each year tens of thousands of men and women gathered, competing to gild its face with gold.

sentences.zh: 俊命焚之，得金悉以償民逋。

translations.literal: Jun ordered it burned; all the gold obtained was used to pay the people's tax arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Jun ordered it burned, and all the gold obtained was used to pay off the people's tax arrears.

sentences.zh: 又毀淫祠三百六十區，皆撤其材修學宮。

translations.literal: He also destroyed three hundred sixty illicit shrines and used their timber to repair the Confucian schools.
translations.idiomatic: He also destroyed three hundred sixty illicit shrines and used their timber to repair the Confucian schools.

sentences.zh: 幹崖土舍刀怕愈欲奪從子宣撫官，劫其印數年。

translations.literal: The native chieftain Daobayu of Ganyai wished to seize his nephew's pacification commissioner's post and had held the seal for years.
translations.idiomatic: Daobayu, a native chieftain of Ganyai, wished to seize his nephew's post as pacification commissioner and had held the seal for years.

sentences.zh: 俊檄諭之，遂歸印。

translations.literal: Jun issued a proclamation admonishing him, and the seal was returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jun issued a proclamation admonishing him, and the seal was returned.

sentences.zh: 進按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年調湖廣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 以雨雪災異上疏陳時政得失。

translations.literal: On grounds of rain, snow, and calamitous signs, he memorialized on the gains and losses of current policy.
translations.idiomatic: Citing rain, snow, and other calamitous signs, he memorialized on the strengths and failings of current policy.

sentences.zh: 又言德安、安陸建王府及增修吉府，工役浩繁，財費巨萬，民不堪命。

translations.literal: He also said that building princely estates at De'an and Anlu and expanding the Ji princely establishment entailed vast labor and expenditures of tens of thousands; the people could not bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that building princely estates at De'an and Anlu and expanding the Ji princely establishment entailed vast labor and expenditures in the tens of thousands, and the people could not bear the burden.

sentences.zh: 乞循寧、襄、德府故事，一切省儉，勿用琉璃及白石雕闌，請著為例。

translations.literal: He asked to follow the precedents of the Ning, Xiang, and De establishments, economize in all respects, not use glazed tile or white-stone carved balustrades, and asked that this be made a fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to follow the precedents of the Ning, Xiang, and De establishments, economize in all respects, not use glazed tile or white-stone carved balustrades, and asked that this be established as a fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: [The emperor] did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not comply.

sentences.zh: 九年引疾，不待報徑歸。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he cited illness and returned home without awaiting a reply.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he cited illness and went home without waiting for a reply.

sentences.zh: 久之，薦起廣東右布政使，不拜。

translations.literal: After a long while he was recommended and summoned as Right Administrative Commissioner of Guangdong; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was recommended and summoned to serve as Right Administrative Commissioner of Guangdong, but he did not accept.

sentences.zh: 起南京右僉都御史，督操江。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing to oversee river defense operations.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing to oversee river-defense operations.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月朔，陜西、山西地震水湧。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the fourteenth year, Shaanxi and Shanxi suffered earthquakes and flooding.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the first month of the fourteenth year, Shaanxi and Shanxi were struck by earthquakes and flooding.

sentences.zh: 疏述古宮闈、外戚、內侍、柄臣之禍；

translations.literal: In a memorial he recounted the calamities of old from palace women, consort kin, inner attendants, and power-holding ministers;
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he recounted the calamities of old wrought by palace women, consort kin, inner attendants, and power-holding ministers;

sentences.zh: 乞罷齋醮，減織造，清役占，汰冗員，止工作，省供應，應賞賜，戒逸欲，遠佞幸，親賢人。

translations.literal: He asked to abolish Daoist rites, reduce textile manufacture, clear illegal corvée claims, eliminate redundant posts, halt construction, economize on provisions, restrain bestowals, guard against dissipation, keep sycophants at a distance, and be close to worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to abolish Daoist rites, reduce textile manufacture, clear illegal corvée claims, eliminate redundant posts, halt construction, economize on provisions, restrain gifts and bestowals, guard against dissipation, keep sycophants at a distance, and draw close to worthy men.

sentences.zh: 又請豫教皇儲，恩薦侍郎謝鐸，少卿儲瓘、楊廉，致仕副使曹時中，處士劉閔堪輔導。

translations.literal: He also asked that the heir be instructed in advance and graciously recommended Vice Minister Xie Duo, Vice Directors Chu Jin and Yang Lian, retired Vice Commissioner Cao Shizhong, and recluse Liu Min as worthy tutors.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the heir be given advance instruction and graciously recommended Vice Minister Xie Duo, Vice Directors Chu Jin and Yang Lian, retired Vice Commissioner Cao Shizhong, and the recluse Liu Min as men fit to serve as tutors.

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: The report was received and noted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was acknowledged.

sentences.zh: 已，屢疏乞休，薦時中自代。

translations.literal: Thereafter he repeatedly memorialized asking to retire and recommended Shizhong to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: After that he repeatedly memorialized asking to retire and recommended Cao Shizhong as his successor.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: Not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 江西新昌民王武為盜，巡撫韓邦問不能靖，命俊巡視。

translations.literal: In Jiangxi, a commoner of Xinchang named Wang Wu became a bandit; Grand Coordinator Han Bangwen could not pacify the region, and Jun was ordered to inspect it.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangxi, a Xinchang commoner named Wang Wu turned bandit; Grand Coordinator Han Bangwen could not restore order, and Jun was ordered to inspect the province.

sentences.zh: 身入武巢，武請自效，悉擒賊黨。

translations.literal: He went in person into Wu's lair; Wu asked to serve in merit, and all the bandit partisans were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Jun entered Wang Wu's stronghold in person; Wu offered to redeem himself through service, and every member of the band was captured.

sentences.zh: 詔即以俊代邦問，俊引朱熹代唐仲友、包拯代宋祁事，力辭。

translations.literal: An edict immediately appointed Jun to replace Bangwen; Jun cited Zhu Xi replacing Tang Zhongyou and Bao Zheng replacing Song Qi and strenuously declined.
translations.idiomatic: An edict immediately appointed Jun to replace Bangwen, but Jun cited the precedents of Zhu Xi declining to replace Tang Zhongyou and Bao Zheng declining to replace Song Qi and refused the post with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 不允。

translations.literal: Not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 乃更定要約，庶務一新。

translations.literal: Thereupon he revised compacts and renewed all administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then revised local agreements and brought every branch of administration to new order.

sentences.zh: 王府征歲祿，率倍取於民，以俊言大減省。

translations.literal: The princely establishment collected annual stipends, generally taking double from the people; on Jun's recommendation this was greatly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The princely establishment levied annual stipends, routinely taking twice what the people could bear; at Jun's urging the exactions were sharply cut.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠貪暴，俊屢裁抑之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ning, Chen Hao, was greedy and violent; Jun repeatedly checked and restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ning, Chen Hao, was greedy and brutal; Jun repeatedly curbed his excesses.

sentences.zh: 王請易琉璃瓦，費二萬。

translations.literal: The prince requested to replace the glazed tiles at a cost of twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The prince asked to replace the glazed roof tiles at a cost of twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 俊言宜如舊，毋涉叔段京鄙之求，吳王幾杖之賜。

translations.literal: Jun said it should remain as before and must not touch upon Duke Shu's request at Jing of old or the gift of a cane stool to the King of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Jun argued that things should stay as they were and that the prince must not press demands like those of Duke Shu at Jing or accept gifts like the cane stool granted the King of Wu.

sentences.zh: 王怒，伺其過，無所得。

translations.literal: The prince was enraged, watched for his faults, and found nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was furious and watched for a chance to catch him out, but found no fault.

sentences.zh: 會俊以聖節按部，遂劾奏之，停俸三月。

translations.literal: When Jun happened to be touring the jurisdiction on the emperor's birthday, he memorialized impeaching the prince, and [Jun's] salary was suspended for three months.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun happened to be on an inspection tour for the imperial birthday, he memorialized impeaching the prince and was himself suspended from salary for three months.

sentences.zh: 尋以母憂歸。

translations.literal: Soon after he returned home on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，言官交薦，江西人在朝者合疏乞還俊。

translations.literal: When the Wuzong Emperor ascended, censors recommended him one after another, and Jiangxi natives at court jointly memorialized asking that Jun be returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuzong Emperor took the throne, censors recommended him in succession, and Jiangxi officials at court jointly memorialized asking that Jun be recalled.

sentences.zh: 乃進右副都御史，再撫江西，遭父憂不果。

translations.literal: He was then promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and again appointed to pacify Jiangxi, but the plan did not come to pass when he suffered his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and again appointed to pacify Jiangxi, but mourning for his father prevented him from taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 正德四年起撫四川。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengde he was recalled to pacify Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhengde he was recalled to serve as grand coordinator of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 眉州人劉烈倡亂，敗而逃，諸不逞假其名剽掠。

translations.literal: Liu Lie of Meizhou raised a rebellion; defeated, he fled, and various unruly men plundered under his name.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lie of Meizhou stirred up rebellion; when he was defeated and fled, lawless men everywhere looted in his name.

sentences.zh: 俊繪形捕，莫能得。

translations.literal: Jun had portraits drawn for capture but could not apprehend him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun circulated wanted portraits but could not capture him.

sentences.zh: 會保寧賊藍廷瑞、鄢本恕、廖惠等繼起，勢益張，轉寇巴州。

translations.literal: Then bandits of Baoning—Lan Tingrui, Yan Benshu, Liao Hui, and others—rose in succession; their force grew ever stronger and they turned to raid Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Baoning bandits Lan Tingrui, Yan Benshu, Liao Hui, and others rose one after another; their power swelled until they turned to raid Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 猝遇之華壟，單輿抵其營，譬曉利害，賊羅拜約降。

translations.literal: Suddenly encountering them at Hualong, he went alone in a carriage to their camp, explained the gains and losses, and the bandits bowed in a circle and agreed to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When he suddenly encountered them at Hualong, he drove alone into their camp, explained what they stood to gain or lose, and the bandits bowed all around and pledged to surrender.

sentences.zh: 淫雨失期，復叛去，攻陷通江。

translations.literal: Heavy rains caused them to miss the deadline; they rebelled again and seized Tongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Endless rain kept them from keeping their deadline; they rebelled again and overran Tongjiang.

sentences.zh: 俊擊敗之龍灘河，遣知府張敏等追敗之門鎮子，遂擒廖惠。

translations.literal: Jun defeated them at Longtan River, sent Prefect Zhang Min and others in pursuit to defeat them at Menzhenzi, and thus captured Liao Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Jun routed them at Longtan River, sent Prefect Zhang Min and others in pursuit to defeat them at Menzhenzi, and captured Liao Hui.

sentences.zh: 而廷瑞奔陜西西鄉，越漢中三十六盤，至大巴山。

translations.literal: Tingrui fled to Xixiang in Shaanxi, crossed the Thirty-Six Bends of Hanzhong, and reached the Daba Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Tingrui fled to Xixiang in Shaanxi, crossed the Thirty-Six Bends of Hanzhong, and made for the Daba Mountains.

sentences.zh: 官軍追及，復大破之。

translations.literal: Government troops caught up and again routed them thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops caught up and broke them again.

sentences.zh: 遂移師擊瀘州賊曹甫，且遣人招諭。

translations.literal: He then shifted his army to strike the Luzhou bandit Cao Fu and also sent men to summon and admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved his army against the Luzhou bandit Cao Fu while also sending envoys to summon and persuade him.

sentences.zh: 甫佯聽令，使弟琯劫如故。

translations.literal: Fu pretended to obey, but had his younger brother Guan continue plundering as before.
translations.idiomatic: Fu pretended to submit, but had his younger brother Guan go on raiding as before.

sentences.zh: 指揮李蔭斬琯首，賊遂移江津。

translations.literal: Commander Li Yin beheaded Guan; the bandits then moved to Jiangjin.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Li Yin cut off Guan's head, and the bandits shifted their base to Jiangjin.

sentences.zh: 分七營，將攻重慶。

translations.literal: They divided into seven camps and were about to attack Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: They split into seven camps and prepared to strike Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 俊發酉陽、播州土兵助蔭，以元日掩破其四營。

translations.literal: Jun dispatched native troops from Youyang and Bozhou to assist Yin, and on New Year's Day launched a surprise attack that broke four of their camps.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent native troops from Youyang and Bozhou to reinforce Yin and, on New Year's Day, launched a surprise attack that smashed four of their camps.

sentences.zh: 賊遁入民家，焚之盡斃。

translations.literal: The bandits fled into commoners' houses; [the troops] burned them and killed all inside.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits hid in civilian homes; the troops burned the houses and killed everyone inside.

sentences.zh: 乘勝搗老營，指揮汪洋等中伏死。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory to storm their main camp, Commander Wang Yang and others fell into an ambush and died.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing their advantage against the main camp, Commander Wang Yang and others walked into an ambush and were killed.

sentences.zh: 蔭復進，去賊十五里。

translations.literal: Yin advanced again, fifteen li from the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yin pushed forward again until he was fifteen li from the bandits.

sentences.zh: 甫以數十騎出，遇蔭兵，敗走。

translations.literal: Fu came out with several dozen horsemen, encountered Yin's troops, and fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Fu rode out with several dozen horsemen, ran into Yin's force, and fled in defeat.

sentences.zh: 官軍乘勝進圍之，俘及焚死者二千有奇。

translations.literal: Government troops pressed the advantage, advanced and besieged them; captives and those burned to death numbered slightly over two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops pressed the attack, closed in, and besieged them; captives and those burned alive numbered slightly more than two thousand.

sentences.zh: 已，本恕、廷瑞為永順土舍彭世麟所擒。

translations.literal: Before long, Benshu and Tingrui were captured by Peng Shilin, a native clerk of Yongshun.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Benshu and Tingrui were seized by Peng Shilin, a native clerk of Yongshun.

sentences.zh: 俊論功進右都御史。

translations.literal: For his merit, Jun was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements, Jun was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 甫黨方四亡命思南，復攻南川、綦江，以窺瀘州。

translations.literal: Fu's partisan Fang Si was an outlaw in Sinan; he again attacked Nanchuan and Qijiang, aiming to threaten Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Fu's follower Fang Si was a fugitive in Sinan; he again struck Nanchuan and Qijiang, probing toward Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 俊益發士兵，令副使何珊、李鉞等敗之去。

translations.literal: Jun dispatched more native soldiers and ordered Vice Commissioners He Shan and Li Yue and others to defeat and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent out more native troops and had Vice Commissioners He Shan and Li Yue and others drive them back.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，璽書獎勵。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, an imperial letter of commendation arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory arrived, the emperor sent a sealed letter of praise.

sentences.zh: 俊在軍，與總督洪鐘議多左。

translations.literal: While in the army, Jun often disagreed with Grand Coordinator Hong Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign, Jun often found himself at odds with Grand Coordinator Hong Zhong.

sentences.zh: 中貴子弟欲冒從軍功，輒禁止。

translations.literal: When sons of favored eunuchs sought to claim military merit fraudulently, he always forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever sons of favored eunuchs tried to pass off false battlefield credit, he blocked them.

sentences.zh: 御史俞緇走避賊，而僉事吳景戰歿。

translations.literal: Censor Yu Zi fled to avoid the bandits, while Assistant Commissioner Wu Jing died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yu Zi ran from the bandits, while Assistant Commissioner Wu Jing fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 緇慚，欲委罪俊，遂劾俊累報首功，賊終不滅；

translations.literal: Zi was ashamed and wished to shift blame onto Jun; he memorialized impeaching Jun for repeatedly reporting severed-head victories while the bandits were never exterminated;
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Zi tried to pin the blame on Jun and memorialized impeaching him for repeatedly reporting severed heads while the bandits were never wiped out;

sentences.zh: 加鑿井毀寺，逐僧徒，迫為賊。

translations.literal: additionally digging wells and destroying temples, expelling monks and forcing them to become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: and for digging wells and tearing down temples, driving out monks and forcing them into banditry.

sentences.zh: 於是俊前後被切責。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jun was severely reprimanded repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was then sharply rebuked again and again.

sentences.zh: 比方四敗，賊且盡，俊辭加秩及賞，乞以舊職歸田。

translations.literal: When Fang Si was defeated, the bandits were nearly exterminated; Jun declined promotion and reward, asking to retire to his fields with his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang Si was beaten, the bandits were nearly gone; Jun refused further promotion and reward and asked to retire to his fields at his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 詔不許辭秩，聽其致仕。

translations.literal: An edict did not permit him to decline the rank but allowed him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: An edict refused his resignation of rank but permitted him to retire from office.

sentences.zh: 言官交請留，不報。

translations.literal: Censors repeatedly asked that he be retained; no response.
translations.idiomatic: Censors repeatedly petitioned that he be kept on, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 俊歸，士民號哭追送。

translations.literal: When Jun returned home, scholars and commoners wept and ran after him to bid farewell.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun went home, scholars and commoners wept and ran after his carriage to see him off.

sentences.zh: 時正德六年十一月也。

translations.literal: It was the eleventh month of the sixth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the eleventh month of the sixth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，起工部尚書，改刑部。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor ascended, Jun was recalled as Minister of Works and transferred to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizong Emperor took the throne, Jun was recalled as Minister of Works and then moved to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 在道數引疾，不許。

translations.literal: En route he repeatedly cited illness; not granted.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he repeatedly pleaded illness, but was not allowed to turn back.

sentences.zh: 因請帝親近儒臣，正其心以出號令，用渾樸為天下先。

translations.literal: He therefore asked the emperor to draw close to Confucian ministers, rectify his heart in issuing commands, and take unadorned simplicity as the model for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore urged the emperor to keep Confucian ministers near, set his heart right before issuing commands, and lead the realm by plain, unadorned example.

sentences.zh: 初詔所革，無遷就以廢公議。

translations.literal: The initial edicts that were revoked should not involve transfers that set aside public consensus.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that the first edicts to be withdrawn should not use reshuffling of appointments to override public opinion.

sentences.zh: 既抵京師，會暑月經筵輟講，舉祖宗勤學故事以諫。

translations.literal: Once he reached the capital, as the lecture hall was suspended in the hot summer months, he remonstrated by citing the ancestral examples of diligent study.
translations.idiomatic: After he reached the capital, the lecture hall was suspended during the summer heat; he remonstrated by citing the ancestral tradition of diligent study.

sentences.zh: 俊時年已七十，寓止朝房，示無久居意。

translations.literal: Jun was then already seventy; he lodged in the court offices, showing he had no intention of staying long.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was already seventy; he took quarters in the court offices to signal that he did not mean to linger.

sentences.zh: 數為帝言親大臣，勤聖學，辨異端，節財用。

translations.literal: He repeatedly spoke to the emperor of drawing close to senior ministers, diligently pursuing sagely learning, distinguishing heterodox teachings, and economizing on expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly urged the emperor to trust senior ministers, pursue the sage's learning, reject heterodox teachings, and tighten spending.

sentences.zh: 朝有大政，必侃侃陳論，中外想望其風采。

translations.literal: When there was great policy at court, he always spoke forthrightly; within and without the court all looked to his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever major policy was at stake, he spoke without flinching, and men inside and outside the court looked to him with hope.

sentences.zh: 中官葛景等奸利事覺，為言官所糾，詔下司禮監察訊。

translations.literal: The corrupt profiteering of inner attendants Ge Jing and others was exposed; impeached by censors, an edict ordered the Directorate of Ceremonial to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The graft of inner attendants Ge Jing and others came to light; after censors impeached them, an edict sent the case to the Directorate of Ceremonial for inquiry.

sentences.zh: 俊言內臣犯法，法司不得訊，是宮府異體也。

translations.literal: Jun said that when inner attendants violated the law, the judicial offices could not interrogate them—this made palace and state separate bodies.
translations.idiomatic: Jun argued that if inner attendants broke the law yet the judicial offices could not try them, palace and state would no longer be one body.

sentences.zh: 乞下法司公訊，以詔平明之治。

translations.literal: He asked that the case be sent down to the judicial offices for public interrogation, to proclaim equitable governance.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the case be handed to the judicial offices for open trial, as a sign of fair and clear rule.

sentences.zh: 都督劉暉下獄，俊當以交結朋黨律，言與許泰同罪，請斬以謝天下。

translations.literal: Grand Defender Liu Hui was imprisoned; Jun argued that under the statute on forming factions he was guilty of the same crime as Xu Tai and asked that he be executed to appease all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Defender Liu Hui was thrown into prison, Jun held that under the law against factional collusion he deserved the same punishment as Xu Tai and should be executed to satisfy the realm.

sentences.zh: 廖鵬、廖鎧、齊佐、王瓛論死，屢詔緩刑，俊乞亟行誅。

translations.literal: Liao Peng, Liao Kai, Qi Zuo, and Wang Huan were sentenced to death; edicts repeatedly deferred execution; Jun asked that the sentence be carried out promptly.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Peng, Liao Kai, Qi Zuo, and Wang Huan had been condemned to death, but edicts repeatedly stayed the execution; Jun pleaded that they be put to death at once.

sentences.zh: 又劾谷大用占民田萬余頃。

translations.literal: He also impeached Gu Dayong for seizing more than ten thousand qing of commoners' farmland.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Gu Dayong for occupying more than ten thousand qing of commoners' farmland.

sentences.zh: 皆不聽。

translations.literal: None of these were heeded.
translations.idiomatic: None of his pleas were accepted.

sentences.zh: 中官崔文家人李陽鳳索匠師宋鈺賄不獲，嗾文杖之幾死，下刑部治未決，而中旨移鎮撫司。

translations.literal: A family retainer of inner attendant Cui Wen, Li Yangfeng, demanded a bribe from master craftsman Song Yu and failed to obtain it; he incited Wen to beat him nearly to death. The case was sent to the Ministry of Justice for trial but was not yet decided when an inner edict transferred it to the Brocade Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yangfeng, a retainer in the household of inner attendant Cui Wen, demanded a bribe from master craftsman Song Yu; when Yu refused, Yangfeng goaded Wen into beating him nearly to death. The Ministry of Justice took the case but had not yet ruled when an inner edict moved it to the Brocade Guard.

sentences.zh: 俊留不遣，力爭不納。

translations.literal: Jun detained the prisoner and would not release him, contending strenuously and refusing to comply.
translations.idiomatic: Jun held the prisoner back and would not hand him over, arguing fiercely and refusing to obey.

sentences.zh: 明日又奏，帝怒責陳狀。

translations.literal: The next day he memorialized again; the emperor angrily ordered him to explain himself.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he memorialized again; the emperor flew into a rage and ordered him to state his case.

sentences.zh: 俊言：「祖宗以刑獄付法司，以緝獲奸盜付鎮撫。

translations.literal: Jun said: "The ancestral emperors entrusted criminal cases to the judicial offices and entrusted the apprehension of traitors and robbers to the Brocade Guard.
