translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "Our ancestral emperors entrusted criminal trials to the judicial offices and the capture of traitors and thieves to the Brocade Guard.

sentences.zh: 訊鞫既得，猶必付法司擬罪。

translations.literal: Once interrogation had obtained results, the case still had to be sent to the judicial offices to determine punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Even after interrogation had yielded a result, the case still had to go to the judicial offices to fix the penalty.

sentences.zh: 未有奪取未定之囚，反付推問者。

translations.literal: Never before has an unresolved prisoner been seized and handed back to the interrogator.
translations.idiomatic: Never before has a prisoner whose case was still undecided been snatched away and returned to the very office that had been questioning him.

sentences.zh: 文先朝漏奸，罪不容誅，茲復幹內降。

translations.literal: Wen escaped punishment for treason in the previous reign; his crime brooked no execution, and now again he interferes with an inner edict.
translations.idiomatic: Wen slipped through punishment for treason in the previous reign—a crime that should not have been spared—and now again he meddles by way of an inner edict.

sentences.zh: 臣不忍朝廷百五十年紀綱，為此輩壞亂。」

translations.literal: Your subject cannot bear to see the institutions of a hundred fifty years of the court ruined and thrown into disorder by such men."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject cannot bear to watch a hundred and fifty years of court discipline torn apart by men like these."

sentences.zh: 帝憚其言直，乃不問。

translations.literal: The emperor, deterred by his blunt words, let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, checked by his blunt honesty, dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 俊以耆德起田間，持正不避嫌，既屢見格，遂乞致仕。

translations.literal: Summoned from the fields for his aged virtue, Jun held to rectitude without shunning suspicion; repeatedly overruled, he then asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Called back from retirement for his aged virtue, Jun stood on principle without dodging blame; after repeated rebuffs he asked to leave office.

sentences.zh: 詔加太子太保，給驛賜隸廩如制。

translations.literal: An edict added the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted post horses, and bestowed stipends according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict added the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted him courier horses, and gave him stipends as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 俊數爭「大禮」，與楊廷和合。

translations.literal: Jun repeatedly disputed the "Grand Rites" affair and sided with Yang Tinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Jun repeatedly contested the Grand Rites controversy and stood with Yang Tinghe.

sentences.zh: 嘗上言推尊所生有不容已之情，有不可易之禮，因輯堯、舜至宋理宗事凡十條，以上。

translations.literal: He once memorialized that honoring one's biological parents involved feelings that could not be restrained and rites that could not be altered; he compiled ten precedents from Yao and Shun down to Emperor Lizong of Song and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized that honoring one's biological parents rested on feelings that could not be suppressed and rites that could not be changed; he gathered ten precedents from Yao and Shun down to Emperor Lizong of Song and submitted them.

sentences.zh: 及「大禮」議定，得罪者或杖死。

translations.literal: When the "Grand Rites" debate was settled, some who had offended were beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Grand Rites debate was settled, some who had offended died under the beating staff.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，俊從病中上書言：「古者鞭撲之刑，辱之而已，非欲糜爛其體膚而致之死也，又非所以加於士大夫也。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year, Jun memorialized from his sickbed, saying: "In antiquity the punishment of the whip was only meant to humiliate, not to mangle the body and bring about death, nor was it meant to be applied to scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year, Jun wrote from his sickbed: "In antiquity the rod and whip were punishments of shame only—they were not meant to flay a man's flesh until he died, nor were they meant for the scholar-official class.

sentences.zh: 成化時，臣及見廷杖二三臣，率容厚棉底衣，重氈疊裹，然且沈臥，久乃得痊。

translations.literal: During the Chenghua reign, your subject personally saw two or three ministers beaten at court; they generally wore thick padded undergarments and layers of heavy felt, yet still collapsed and lay prostrate, and only after a long while recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chenghua reign I myself saw two or three ministers beaten at court; even though they wore thick padded underclothes and heavy felt wrappings, they still collapsed and could not rise for a long time.

sentences.zh: 正德朝，逆瑾竊權，始令去衣，致末年多杖死。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign, the rebel Liu Jin usurped power and first ordered them stripped before beating; by the end of the reign many died under the staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengde reign the usurper Liu Jin first ordered men stripped before the beating, and by the end of that reign many died under the staff.

sentences.zh: 臣又見成化、弘治時，惟叛逆、妖言、劫盜下詔獄，始命打問。

translations.literal: Your subject also saw that during Chenghua and Hongzhi, only cases of rebellion, heterodox speech, and robbery were sent to the imperial prison before beating during interrogation was ordered.
translations.idiomatic: I also saw that under Chenghua and Hongzhi, only rebels, purveyors of heterodox speech, and robbers were sent to the imperial prison before interrogation under beating was ordered.

sentences.zh: 他犯但言送問而已。

translations.literal: For other offenses one need only say 'send for questioning.'
translations.idiomatic: For other crimes the order was simply to send the case for questioning.

sentences.zh: 今一概打問，亦非故事。

translations.literal: To subject all cases uniformly to beating during interrogation is also not precedent.
translations.idiomatic: To beat every case during interrogation alike is likewise no established practice.

sentences.zh: 自去歲舊臣斥逐殆盡，朝署為空。

translations.literal: Since last year the old ministers have been expelled nearly to exhaustion, and the court offices stand empty.
translations.idiomatic: Since last year the senior ministers have been driven out almost to the last man, and the halls of government stand empty.

sentences.zh: 乞聖明留念，既去者禮致，未去者慰留。

translations.literal: I ask Your Sagely Clarity to take heed: treat with ceremony those who have left, and comfort and retain those who remain.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Sagely Clarity to take thought: honor with ceremony those who have gone, and comfort and keep those who remain.

sentences.zh: 碩德重望如羅欽順、王守仁、呂柟、魯鐸輩，宜列置左右。

translations.literal: Men of great virtue and weighty reputation such as Luo Qinshun, Wang Shouren, Lü Nan, and Lu Duo should be placed at Your side.
translations.idiomatic: Men of towering virtue and reputation—Luo Qinshun, Wang Shouren, Lü Nan, Lu Duo, and the like—should be set at Your side.

sentences.zh: 臣衰病待盡，無復他望，敢效古人遺表之意，敬布犬馬之心。」

translations.literal: Your subject, declining with illness and awaiting the end, has no further hope; I dare emulate the intent of the ancients' final memorials and lay bare the heart of a loyal hound and horse."
translations.idiomatic: I am worn out by age and illness and await the end; I have no other wish. I dare only follow the spirit of the ancients' deathbed memorials and offer this loyal servant's heart."

sentences.zh: 帝但下所司而已。

translations.literal: The emperor merely referred the matter to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor simply referred the memorial to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 又明年，疾革，復上書請懋學隆孝，任賢納諫，保躬導和，且預辭身後恤典，遂卒。

translations.literal: The following year, as his illness became critical, he memorialized again asking that study be vigorously pursued and filial piety honored, that worthy men be employed and remonstrance accepted, that the body be preserved and harmony cultivated; he also declined in advance posthumous honors, and then died.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, as his illness turned grave, he memorialized again urging earnest study and exalted filial piety, the employment of worthy men and acceptance of remonstrance, self-restraint and the cultivation of harmony; he also declined in advance any posthumous honors, and then died.

sentences.zh: 年七十六。

translations.literal: He was seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy-six years old.

sentences.zh: 後一年，《明倫大典》成，追論俊附和廷和，削其官，其子達以士禮葬之。

translations.literal: A year later, when the Compendium of Human Relations was completed, Jun was posthumously charged with siding with Tinghe; his office was stripped, and his son Da buried him with the rites due a scholar.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, when the Minglun Compendium was completed, Jun was posthumously condemned for siding with Tinghe; his rank was stripped, and his son Da buried him with the rites due a private gentleman.

sentences.zh: 俊歷事四朝，抗辭敢諫，以禮進退，始終一節。

translations.literal: Jun served four reigns, spoke out in remonstrance, advanced and withdrew according to ritual, and maintained one consistent integrity throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Jun served four reigns, spoke boldly in remonstrance, entered and left office according to ritual, and held one unbroken standard to the end.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，復官，贈少保，謚貞肅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing his office was restored; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Guardian and given the posthumous title Zhensu.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Longqing his rank was restored; he was posthumously made Junior Guardian and given the posthumous name Zhensu, Upright and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 達，正德九年進士。

translations.literal: Da became a jinshi in the ninth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: Da passed the jinshi examination in the ninth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 官至南京吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He reached the post of Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 工篆籀，能古文。

translations.literal: He was skilled in seal and large seal script and versed in ancient-style prose.
translations.idiomatic: He was accomplished in seal and large seal script and wrote well in the ancient prose style.

sentences.zh: 張黻，吉水人。

translations.literal: Zhang Fu, a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu was from Jishui.

sentences.zh: 成化八年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the eighth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 歷知涪州、宿州，介特不避權貴。

translations.literal: He successively served as prefect of Fuzhou and Suzhou, upright and independent, never shying from the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Fuzhou and Suzhou, standing apart and refusing to yield to the powerful.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，俊蒙顯擢，而黻老不用。

translations.literal: During Hongzhi, Jun received conspicuous promotion, while Fu, now old, went unused.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign, Lin Jun was prominently promoted, but Zhang Fu, though aged, received no appointment.

sentences.zh: 王恕為之請，特予誥命。

translations.literal: Wang Shu interceded on his behalf, and he was specially granted an edict of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu petitioned on his behalf, and the court specially granted him an honorary patent of appointment.

sentences.zh: 金獻民，字舜舉，綿州人。

translations.literal: Jin Xianmin, courtesy name Shunju, was a native of Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Xianmin, styled Shunju, was from Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 成化二十年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the twentieth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twentieth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 除行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed as a palace messenger.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a palace messenger.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，選授御史，按雲南、順天，並著風裁。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi, he was selected and appointed supervising censor, investigating Yunnan and Shuntian, and in both assignments distinguished himself by integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi he was chosen as a supervising censor and sent to inspect Yunnan and Shuntian; in both posts he earned a reputation for uncompromising discipline.

sentences.zh: 出為天津副使，歷湖廣按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred out to serve as vice commissioner of Tianjin and subsequently served as surveillance commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital to serve as vice commissioner at Tianjin and later rose to surveillance commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 正德初，劉瑾亂政，追坐獻民勘天津地不實，與巡撫柳應辰等械系詔獄，斥為民。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde, Liu Jin threw the government into disorder; Xianmin was retroactively charged with inaccurately surveying Tianjin land, and together with Grand Coordinator Liu Yingchen and others was shackled and imprisoned in the imperial prison, then reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengde, with Liu Jin corrupting the government, Xianmin was charged retroactively with falsifying his survey of Tianjin lands; he and Grand Coordinator Liu Yingchen and others were clapped in irons and thrown into the imperial prison, then stripped of office and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又坐湖廣事，再下獄，罰贖歸。

translations.literal: Before long, he was again implicated in Huguang affairs, imprisoned a second time, fined, and sent home after paying ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was implicated again in a Huguang case, jailed once more, fined, and allowed to return home on payment of redemption.

sentences.zh: 逾年，又以瀏陽民劉道隆獄讞不實，罰米輸塞下。

translations.literal: After a year, because the judgment in the case of Liu Daolong, a commoner of Liuyang, was found false, he was fined grain to be delivered to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was punished again when a verdict he had passed in the case of Liu Daolong, a man of Liuyang, proved unsound; he was required to pay a fine in grain for delivery to the frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，起貴州按察使。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, Xianmin was reinstated as surveillance commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's execution he was recalled to serve as surveillance commissioner of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 擢僉都御史，巡撫延綏，歷南京刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Yan-sui, and later served as minister of justice at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Yan-sui, eventually serving as minister of justice at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 錦衣百戶俞賢，中官泰養子也，以中旨管事，諫官爭之。

translations.literal: Yu Xian, a company commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard and adopted son of the eunuch Tai, was put in charge of affairs by secret imperial order; remonstrating officials contested this.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xian, a centurion in the Embroidered Uniform Guard and the adopted son of the eunuch Tai, had been given administrative duties by secret edict; censorial officials protested vigorously.

sentences.zh: 獻民言：「祖宗有舊制，孝廟有禁例，陛下登極有明詔。

translations.literal: Xianmin said: "The ancestral house has old institutions, the Xiaozong emperor left prohibitory precedents, and when Your Majesty ascended the throne there was a clear edict.
translations.idiomatic: Xianmin memorialized: "Our ancestors established fixed regulations; the Xiaozong emperor issued explicit prohibitions; and when Your Majesty took the throne you proclaimed clear edicts.

sentences.zh: 賢無公家庸，又非泰子姓，猥以廝養竊名器，紊棨典章，不可之大者。

translations.literal: Yu Xian holds no public post, nor is he Tai's own surname; yet basely, as a groom's reared servant, he usurps official titles and disorderly defiles the canon of regulations—nothing could be more impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xian holds no legitimate government post and is not even surnamed Tai; that a servant raised in the inner quarters should usurp rank and disorder the institutions of state is an offense of the gravest kind.

sentences.zh: 宜納諫官言。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should accept the remonstrators' words."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty ought to accept the censors' advice."

sentences.zh: 弗聽。

translations.literal: The emperor refused to listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 錦衣副千戶李全、王邦奇等以冒濫汰去，至是奏辨不已，下部覆議。

translations.literal: Li Quan, Wang Bangqi, and other deputy battalion commanders of the Embroidered Uniform Guard had been removed for illicit promotion; now they continually memorialized in their own defense, and the matter was sent down to the ministries for reconsideration.
translations.idiomatic: Li Quan, Wang Bangqi, and other deputy chiliarchs of the Embroidered Uniform Guard had been purged for unmerited advancement; they now submitted endless petitions in their own defense, and the case was referred to the ministries for review.

sentences.zh: 獻民言：「全等足不履行陣而坐論首功，身不隸公家而躐躋顯秩。

translations.literal: Xianmin said: "Quan and the rest whose feet never trod the battle line yet sit discussing top merit, whose persons are not enrolled in public service yet leap to conspicuous rank.
translations.idiomatic: Xianmin argued: "Men like Quan never set foot on a battlefield yet claim first honors for merit; they belong to no proper government roster yet vault into high rank.

sentences.zh: 陛下登極，汰去者三百余人，人心稱快。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty ascended the throne, more than three hundred were purged, and popular sentiment rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty came to the throne you removed more than three hundred such men, to the relief and approval of the realm.

sentences.zh: 萬一幸端再啟，則前詔皆虛，將來奏擾，有何紀極。」

translations.literal: Should this opening of loopholes occur again by any chance, then the prior edicts become empty; future petition clamor—where would be its limit?"
translations.idiomatic: If such abuses reopen even once, your earlier edicts will be rendered void; how will you ever set a limit to the petitions and disturbances that follow?"

sentences.zh: 帝竟授全等試百戶。

translations.literal: The emperor ultimately granted Quan and the others probationary company commanderships.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nevertheless appointed Quan and his fellows probationary centurions.

sentences.zh: 獻民復奏曰：「令出惟行勿惟反。

translations.literal: Xianmin memorialized again: "When an order is issued, execute it—do not reverse it.
translations.idiomatic: Xianmin memorialized again: "When an edict is issued, it must be carried out and not withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 今以小人奏辨，一旦復官九十余人，徇左右私，壞祖宗法，竊為陛下惜之。

translations.literal: Now on the petitions of petty men, more than ninety have been reinstated at a stroke; indulging the private interests of those at your side, you damage ancestral law—I privately grieve for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Now, on the word of unworthy petitioners, more than ninety have been restored to office overnight; this favors your intimates, breaks ancestral law, and I must lament it on Your Majesty's behalf.

sentences.zh: 明旨不許夤緣管事，而奔競已成風矣；

translations.literal: A clear edict forbade currying favor to manage affairs, yet frantic scrambling has already become the norm;
translations.idiomatic: Your explicit decree forbade using connections to obtain administrative posts, yet frantic lobbying has already become the custom;

sentences.zh: 不許比例陳乞，而奏擾已踵至矣。

translations.literal: Petitioning by proportional precedent was not permitted, yet memorial clamor has already followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: You forbade petitions citing precedent for rank, yet a torrent of such memorials has already followed.

sentences.zh: 誰生厲階，至今為梗。

translations.literal: Who raised this source of trouble, which even now remains an obstruction?
translations.idiomatic: Who opened this path of harm that still blocks good government today?

sentences.zh: 望仍斥全等，以息人言，消天變。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will again dismiss Quan and the rest, to quiet public talk and dispel heavenly portents."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Quan and his fellows be dismissed again, to still public criticism and avert the signs of heaven's displeasure."

sentences.zh: 言官任洛等亦以為言，不聽。

translations.literal: Censorial officials such as Ren Luo also spoke likewise; the emperor refused to listen.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials such as Ren Luo spoke to the same effect; the emperor would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 會寧夏總兵官種勛行賂京師，偵事者獲其籍，獻民名在焉。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhong Xun, regional commander of Ningxia, had bribed persons in the capital; investigators seized his register, and Xianmin's name was among them.
translations.idiomatic: When investigators seized the account books of Zhong Xun, regional commander of Ningxia, who had been bribing officials in the capital, Xianmin's name appeared among the recipients.

sentences.zh: 給事蔡經、御史高世魁等交章劾之，獻民因引疾歸。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Cai Jing, censor Gao Shikui, and others submitted memorial after memorial impeaching him; Xianmin therefore cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Cai Jing, the censor Gao Shikui, and others submitted joint impeachments; Xianmin took the occasion to request leave on grounds of illness and retire.

sentences.zh: 居二年，邦奇訐前尚書彭澤，詞連獻民，逮下刑部獄。

translations.literal: After two years, Bangqi denounced former minister Peng Ze; the charges implicated Xianmin, who was arrested and imprisoned in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Wang Bangqi accused the former minister Peng Ze and implicated Xianmin as well; Xianmin was arrested and held in the Ministry of Justice prison.

sentences.zh: 法司劾獻民奉命專征，未至其地，掠功妄報。

translations.literal: The judiciary impeached Xianmin for having received orders for an exclusive campaign, not yet reaching the place, yet seizing credit and filing false reports.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial authorities charged that Xianmin, though ordered on an independent military expedition, had not reached the field yet had falsely claimed credit in his reports.

sentences.zh: 失大臣體，宜奪職閑住，削其世蔭。

translations.literal: He had failed the dignity of a great minister; his office should be stripped and he should live in retirement; his hereditary privilege should be revoked.
translations.idiomatic: He had disgraced the conduct expected of a senior minister; he should be stripped of office and confined to private life, and his hereditary privilege annulled.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 初，「大禮」議起，獻民數偕廷臣疏爭。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the "Great Rites" controversy arose, Xianmin several times joined court ministers in memorials of protest.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Great Rites controversy erupted, Xianmin repeatedly joined the court ministers in memorial protests.

sentences.zh: 及左順門哭諫，又與徐文華倡之。

translations.literal: When the left Shun Gate weeping remonstrance occurred, he again joined Xu Wenhua in leading it.
translations.idiomatic: At the left Shun Gate remonstrance, when officials wept and protested, he again took the lead with Xu Wenhua.

sentences.zh: 帝由此不悅，卒得罪。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased on this account and in the end Xianmin fell afoul of the law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took lasting offense, and Xianmin eventually paid for it.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈恤如制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, posthumous honors and pensions were granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Longqing he received posthumous honors and compensation according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 秦金，字國聲，無錫人。

translations.literal: Qin Jin, courtesy name Guosheng, was a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Jin, styled Guosheng, was from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the sixth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事，歷郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and successively served as bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and rose through the ranks to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 正德初，遷河南提學副使，改右參政。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde, he was transferred to vice education intendant of Henan and then changed to right administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengde he was transferred to vice education intendant of Henan, then appointed right administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 守開封，破趙鐩於陳橋。

translations.literal: Defending Kaifeng, he defeated Zhao Zhen at Chenqiao.
translations.idiomatic: While defending Kaifeng he routed Zhao Zhen at Chenqiao.

sentences.zh: 歷山東左、右布政使。

translations.literal: He successively served as left and right provincial administration commissioners of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as left and right provincial administration commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 承寇躪後，與巡撫趙璜共拊循，瘡痍始起。

translations.literal: After the devastation of bandit raids, together with Grand Coordinator Zhao Huang he jointly soothed and nurtured the people, and the wounds of the land at last began to heal.
translations.idiomatic: After the ravages of marauders, he and Grand Coordinator Zhao Huang worked together to restore order and relief, and the shattered province slowly began to recover.

sentences.zh: 九年擢右副都御史，巡撫湖廣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 諸王府所據山場湖蕩，皆奏還之官。

translations.literal: Mountain tracts and lake marshes held by the various princely establishments were all memorialized for return to government control.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for the return to government control of hills, lakes, and marshes seized by the various princely establishments.

sentences.zh: 降盜賀璋、羅大洪復叛，討平之。

translations.literal: The surrendered bandits He Zhang and Luo Dahong rebelled again; he campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhang and Luo Dahong, bandits who had surrendered, rebelled again; he put down their revolt.

sentences.zh: 郴州桂陽瑤龔福全稱王，金先後破寨八十余，斬首二千級，擒福全及其黨劉福興等。

translations.literal: Gong Fuquan, a Yao chieftain of Guiyang in Chenzhou, declared himself king; Jin successively stormed more than eighty stockades, beheaded two thousand, and captured Fuquan and his follower Liu Fuxing and others.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Fuquan, a Yao leader of Guiyang in Chenzhou who proclaimed himself king, was overcome when Jin captured more than eighty strongholds, took two thousand heads, and seized Fuquan and his lieutenant Liu Fuxing among others.

sentences.zh: 錄功，增俸一級，蔭錦衣世百戶，力辭得請。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded; his salary grade was raised one step and a hereditary centurion in the Embroidered Uniform Guard was granted as privilege; he forcefully declined and his refusal was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were registered: he was given a raise of one salary grade and the hereditary privilege of a centurion in the Embroidered Uniform Guard, but he strenuously declined and was permitted to do so.

sentences.zh: 入為戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，改吏部。

translations.literal: When the Shizong emperor acceded, Jin was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Qin Jin was moved to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 言官論金無人倫鑒，復改戶部，轉左，署部事。

translations.literal: Censorial officials argued that Jin lacked judgment in human relations; he was again transferred to Revenue, then to the left vice ministership, acting as head of the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials criticized him for poor judgment of character; he was shifted back to the Ministry of Revenue, promoted to left vice minister, and placed in charge of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 外戚邵喜乞莊田，金述祖制，請按治。

translations.literal: The consort kin Shao Xi requested estate lands; Jin cited ancestral institutions and asked that the matter be investigated and punished.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial in-law Shao Xi petitioned for crown estate lands, Jin cited ancestral precedent and called for an investigation.

sentences.zh: 帝宥喜，命都察院禁如制。

translations.literal: The emperor pardoned Xi and ordered the Censorate to enforce the prohibition according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor excused Shao Xi but ordered the Censorate to uphold the prohibition as before.

sentences.zh: 中旨各宮仍置皇莊，遣官校分督。

translations.literal: By secret edict, each palace establishment was again to maintain imperial estates, and official runners were dispatched to supervise them separately.
translations.idiomatic: By secret edict the palace establishments were again allowed imperial estates, with runner-officials sent to oversee them.

sentences.zh: 金言：「西漢盛時以苑囿賦貧民，今奈何剝民以益上。

translations.literal: Jin said: "At the height of the Western Han, parklands were assigned to the poor; how can we now strip the people to enrich the throne?
translations.idiomatic: Jin memorialized: "In the flourishing Western Han, imperial parks were granted to the poor; how can we now levy on the people to swell the imperial purse?

sentences.zh: 乞勘正德間額外侵占者，悉歸其主，而盡撤管莊之人。」

translations.literal: I ask that encroachments beyond quota during the Zhengde years be surveyed; all should be returned to their owners, and all overseers of the estates wholly removed."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all lands taken beyond proper limits during the Zhengde reign be surveyed and restored to their rightful owners, and that every estate steward be withdrawn."

sentences.zh: 帝稱善，即從其議。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this and immediately adopted his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended the proposal and adopted it at once.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年擢南京禮部尚書，率諸臣上疏曰：「陛下繼統以來，昭德塞違，勵精圖治，動無過舉，宜召天和，而災眚頻告者，何也？

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing he was promoted to minister of rites at Nanjing; leading the ministers he submitted a memorial saying: "Since Your Majesty succeeded to the throne, you have displayed virtue and blocked wrongdoing, exerted yourself to govern well, and in action made no misstep—heavenly harmony ought to be summoned; yet calamities and portents have repeatedly announced themselves. Why?
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiajing he was elevated to minister of rites at Nanjing and, leading his colleagues, submitted a memorial: "Since Your Majesty inherited the throne you have shown virtue, checked wrongdoing, and labored diligently for good government, without a single improper act; heaven's favor should attend you—yet disasters and warnings have come one after another. Why is this?

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：『靡不有初，鮮克有終。』

translations.literal: The Book of Songs says: 'Nothing is without its beginning, but few bring things to completion.
translations.idiomatic: As the Book of Songs says: 'All things have a beginning, but few are brought to a good end.

sentences.zh: 陛下登極一詔，百度鹹貞，天下拭目望至治。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty ascended the throne, a single edict made every measure upright; the realm wiped its eyes and looked toward perfect order.
translations.idiomatic: Your accession edict set every branch of government aright, and the whole realm looked up in hope of lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 比來多與詔違，百司罔遵，萬民失仰，此詔令不能如初也。

translations.literal: Recently much has contradicted the edicts; the hundred offices fail to obey; the myriad people have lost their pillar—this is that edicts cannot be as at the first.
translations.idiomatic: Lately edicts have often been disregarded, the bureaucracy no longer follows them, and the people have lost their anchor—your commands no longer carry the force they had at the start.

sentences.zh: 即位之初，逐庸回，任耆舊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of your reign, dull and corrupt men were expelled and elders employed.
translations.idiomatic: At first you drove out the mediocre and entrusted the seasoned.

sentences.zh: 比內閣擬旨輒中改，至疏請，徒答溫語，此任賢不能如初也。

translations.literal: Recently when the Grand Secretariat drafts responses, you frequently alter them mid-course; even when ministers submit formal memorials, you reply only with mild words—this is that employing the worthy cannot be as at the first.
translations.idiomatic: Now when the Grand Secretariat drafts replies you often revise them yourself; even formal petitions from your ministers receive only placid answers in return—you no longer trust your worthies as you did at the start.

sentences.zh: 即位之初，聽言如流，朝請暮報。

translations.literal: At the beginning of your reign, you heard proposals like flowing water; requests in the morning were answered by evening.
translations.idiomatic: At first you listened openly, answering memorials submitted at dawn before nightfall.

sentences.zh: 比來事涉戚畹、宦寺，雖九卿執奏，科道交章，皆曰『業經有旨』。

translations.literal: Recently when affairs involve consort kin or eunuchs, even when the nine ministers insist in memorial or censorial officers jointly remonstrate, the answer is always 'there is already an imperial decision.'
translations.idiomatic: Now when matters touch imperial in-laws or eunuchs, even united protest from the nine ministers or the censorate is met with the answer, 'The emperor has already decided.'

sentences.zh: 此聽納不能如初也。

translations.literal: This is that accepting remonstrance cannot be as at the first.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that you no longer heed counsel as you once did.

sentences.zh: 即位之初，凡先朝傳升、乞升等官，一切厘革。

translations.literal: At the beginning of your reign, all officials promoted by transmission or by petition during the prior reign were entirely reformed away.
translations.idiomatic: At first you abolished every rank obtained by irregular promotion or favor during the previous reign.

sentences.zh: 比來恩澤過濫，封拜頻煩。

translations.literal: Recently favors and grace have flowed too freely; enfeoffments and promotions have come in frequent succession.
translations.idiomatic: Lately honors have been dispensed too freely and promotions have multiplied without restraint.

sentences.zh: 此慎名器不能如初也。

translations.literal: This is that guarding the vessel of rank cannot be as at the first.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that you no longer guard official ranks with the care you showed at the start.

sentences.zh: 即位之初，凡奸黨巨惡俱付三法司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of your reign, all great villains of faction were entrusted to the three judicial offices.
translations.idiomatic: At first major criminals and factional ringleaders were left to the three legal tribunals.

sentences.zh: 比來輒下鎮撫。

translations.literal: Recently cases are routinely sent to the Brocade Guard prison.
translations.idiomatic: Now they are routinely handed to the imperial prison under the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 此謹國法不能如初也。

translations.literal: This is that observing the law of the state cannot be as at the first.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that you no longer uphold the law as you did at the start.

sentences.zh: 即位之初，首命戶部減馬房糧芻之半，且令科道官備核馬數。

translations.literal: At the beginning of your reign, you first ordered the Ministry of Revenue to reduce by half the fodder grain for the imperial stables, and further ordered censorial officials to verify horse numbers.
translations.idiomatic: At first you ordered the Ministry of Revenue to halve the fodder allowance for the imperial stud and directed censorial officials to audit the horse rolls.

sentences.zh: 乃因太監閻洪等言，遂寢前詔。

translations.literal: Yet on the word of the eunuchs Yan Hong and others, the prior edict was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: But on the advice of eunuchs such as Yan Hong, that edict was quietly dropped.

sentences.zh: 此恤民瘼不能如初也。

translations.literal: This is that caring for the people's distress cannot be as at the first.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that you no longer attend to the people's hardship as you once did.

sentences.zh: 即位之初，遣斥法王、佛子、國師、禪師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of your reign, the Dharma Kings, Buddha's Sons, State Preceptors, and Meditation Masters were sent away.
translations.idiomatic: At first you expelled the so-called Dharma Kings, Buddha's Sons, state preceptors, and meditation masters.

sentences.zh: 比來於禁地設齋醮。

translations.literal: Recently, within forbidden precincts, fasting altars and Daoist rites have been established.
translations.idiomatic: Now, within the forbidden precincts, fasting ceremonies and Daoist rites are being held.

sentences.zh: 此崇正道不能如初也。

translations.literal: This is that honoring the correct Way cannot be as at the first.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that you no longer uphold the orthodox teaching as you did at first.

sentences.zh: 即位之初，精明充盛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of your reign, clarity and vigor overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: At first your spirit was keen and your energy abundant.

sentences.zh: 比來聖躬弗豫，天顏未復。

translations.literal: Recently the sacred person is unwell; the heavenly countenance has not returned.
translations.idiomatic: Lately Your Majesty's health has faltered and your presence at court has been rare.

sentences.zh: 此嗇精神不能如初也。

translations.literal: This is that conserving the spirit cannot be as at the first.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that you no longer guard your vital energies as you once did.

sentences.zh: 夫初政所以清明者，政出公朝，而左右不預也；

translations.literal: The reason the opening government was lucid was that policy issued from the public court and those at the emperor's side did not participate;
translations.idiomatic: The early reign was clear because policy came from the open court and the emperor's intimates had no part in it;

sentences.zh: 今政所以混混者，政在左右，而外廷不知也。

translations.literal: Now the reason policy is turbid is that policy rests with those at the side, while the outer court knows nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Now it is muddied because policy is made by those at your side while the outer court is kept in the dark.

sentences.zh: 惟政不可一日不在朝廷，惟權不可一日移於左右。

translations.literal: Only government must not for one day be absent from the court; only power must not for one day shift to those at the side.
translations.idiomatic: Government must never for a single day leave the court; power must never for a single day pass into private hands.

sentences.zh: 所謂政在朝廷者，非必皆獨運也。

translations.literal: What is meant by 'policy in the court' is not that the ruler must do everything alone.
translations.idiomatic: When I say that policy belongs in the court, I do not mean that you must govern unaided.

sentences.zh: 股肱有托，耳目有寄，即主威重於九鼎，國勢安於泰山。

translations.literal: With limbs to rely on and ears and eyes entrusted, then the ruler's authority weighs heavier than the nine tripods and the nation's strength rests secure as Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: With worthy ministers as your arms and trusted observers as your eyes and ears, your own authority will stand firm as the nine tripods and the realm will be secure as Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 自古帝王制禦天下，操此術而已。

translations.literal: From ancient times emperors who governed all under heaven used no more than this method.
translations.idiomatic: Every sage ruler who has held the realm has governed by this principle alone.

sentences.zh: 不則宮府之勢隔而信任有所偏，婦寺之情親而聽受有所蔽。

translations.literal: Otherwise the barrier between palace and government is divided and trust is partial; intimacy with women and eunuchs causes listening to be obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the distance between inner and outer courts breeds partial trust, and closeness to consorts and eunuchs deafens the ruler to honest counsel.

sentences.zh: 名曰總攬，而太阿之鐏實移於下矣。」

translations.literal: One is named as gathering all authority, yet in fact the hilt of the Great Axe has shifted downward."
translations.idiomatic: You may be said to hold all power in name, but the handle of imperial authority has passed into other hands."

sentences.zh: 章下禮部，尚書汪俊力勸帝采納，報聞。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Rites; Minister Wang Jun strongly urged the emperor to adopt it; acknowledgment was returned.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the Ministry of Rites; Minister Wang Jun pressed the emperor hard to accept it; the court noted receipt.

sentences.zh: 尋就改兵部。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 孫交去，召為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When Sun Jiao departed, Jin was summoned as minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Jiao left office, Qin Jin was recalled as minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝欲考興獻帝，金偕廷臣伏闕爭，又與何孟春等條張璁建議之非。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to honor the Xingxian emperor; Jin joined court ministers kneeling at the palace gate in protest, and together with He Mengchun and others itemized the errors in Zhang Cong's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sought to elevate his father, the Xingxian emperor, Qin Jin joined the court ministers protesting at the palace gate and, with He Mengchun and others, laid out point by point the faults in Zhang Cong's plan.

sentences.zh: 及上聖母冊，金及趙璜等復不至，帝頻詰讓。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager's investiture was performed, Jin and Zhao Huang and others again did not attend; the emperor repeatedly rebuked and reproached them.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremonial patent for the empress dowager was issued, Qin Jin and Zhao Huang again failed to appear; the emperor repeatedly censured them.

sentences.zh: 金為人樂易。

translations.literal: Qin Jin as a man was easygoing.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Jin was by nature open and affable.

sentences.zh: 及居官，一以廉正自持。

translations.literal: When he held office, he maintained himself wholly by integrity and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: In office he held himself entirely to integrity and rectitude.

sentences.zh: 在戶部，尤孜孜為國。

translations.literal: In the Ministry of Revenue he was especially diligent on the state's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: At the Ministry of Revenue he worked with especial zeal for the state.

sentences.zh: 永福長公主乞寶坻、武清地，以金言頗減。

translations.literal: The Princess Chang of Yongfu begged for land at Baodi and Wuqing; on Qin Jin's words the grant was considerably reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Yongfu Chang requested estates at Baodi and Wuqing, Qin Jin's remonstrance greatly reduced the amount granted.

sentences.zh: 撫寧、山海莊地賜魏國公徐達者，達卒仍歸之官，定國公光祚請之，金執不可。

translations.literal: The Funning and Shanhaiguan manor lands given to Xu Da, Duke of Wei, had on Xu's death reverted to the government; Duke of Ding Guangzuo requested them, and Qin Jin firmly held it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: The Funning and Shanhaiguan estate granted to Xu Da, Duke of Wei, had reverted to the state on his death; when Duke of Ding Guangzuo sought to recover it, Qin Jin firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 給事中黃重、御史張珩等先後爭，金等復以為言，始報許。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Huang Chong, censor Zhang Heng, and others protested in succession; Qin Jin and others again spoke on it, and only then was assent reported.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Huang Chong, censor Zhang Heng, and others protested one after another; when Qin Jin and his colleagues renewed the argument, the emperor at last gave his assent.

sentences.zh: 內府諸監局軍匠至數千人，中官梁諫請下部采金玉珠石，金皆執奏。

translations.literal: Military artisans in the inner-palace directorates numbered in the thousands; the eunuch Liang Jian asked that the ministries procure gold, jade, pearls, and gems; Qin Jin each time memorialized holding firm.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand military artisans served the inner-palace directorates. When the eunuch Liang Jian asked the ministries to procure gold, jade, pearls, and precious stones, Qin Jin submitted firm remonstrances on every point.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 奸人逯俊等乞兩淮鹽引三十萬，帝許之。

translations.literal: Villains such as Lu Jun begged three hundred thousand salt certificates from the Two Huai regions; the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Schemers led by Lu Jun requested three hundred thousand salt vouchers for the Two Huai circuit, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 金力爭不可，積失帝旨。

translations.literal: Qin Jin strove in argument that it could not be done, repeatedly missing the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Jin fought the grant vigorously until he had repeatedly fallen from the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 六年春以考察自陳致仕，馳驛給夫廩如制。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year, on the merit review he petitioned to retire, and post-horses with bearers and stipends were granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year he submitted his retirement at the official review and was sent home with post-horses, bearers, and grain allowance as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 歸五年，薦者不已，乃起南京戶部，疏陳利民六事。

translations.literal: After five years at home, recommenders did not cease; he was then raised to the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue and memorialized six matters benefiting the people.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later, with recommendations unceasing, he was recalled to the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, where he memorialized six measures for the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 尋召為工部尚書，加太子少保。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as minister of works and given the additional title Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon called to be minister of works and given the additional title of Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 帝與張孚敬、李時評諸大臣，以金為賢，頗嫌其老。

translations.literal: The emperor, with Zhang Fuyi and Li Shi evaluating the great ministers, held Qin Jin to be worthy but somewhat disliked his age.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor and Zhang Fuyi and Li Shi reviewed the senior ministers, they judged Qin Jin worthy but thought him rather old.

sentences.zh: 居數月，加太子太保，改南京兵部。

translations.literal: After several months he was given the Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: After a few months he was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 逾歲致仕歸。

translations.literal: After more than a year he retired and returned.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he retired and went home.

sentences.zh: 二十三年卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he died, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-third year of the reign, at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈少保，謚端敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Junior Guardian and the posthumous name Duanmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Junior Guardian with the posthumous name Duanmin, "Upright and Keen."

sentences.zh: 孫柱，以諸生授中書舍人。

translations.literal: Sun Zhu, as a licentiate, was appointed drafting secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sun Zhu, though only a licentiate, was appointed a drafting secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大學士高拱得罪，倉黃去京師，門生皆避匿，柱獨追送百里外。

translations.literal: When Grand Secretary Gao Gong fell from grace and left the capital in haste, his disciples all hid away; Zhu alone pursued and escorted him a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretary Gao Gong fell from favor and fled the capital in panic, his students all kept their distance; Zhu alone followed him and saw him off a hundred li beyond the city.

sentences.zh: 吳中行疏論張居正奪情，被杖下詔獄。

translations.literal: Wu Zhongxing memorialized attacking Zhang Juzheng's seizure of mourning; he was beaten with the rod and sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhongxing submitted a memorial condemning Zhang Juzheng for clinging to office during mourning and was flogged and thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 柱挾醫視湯藥，遂忤居正，遷魯府審理。

translations.literal: Zhu brought a physician to tend his medicine and soup; he thereby offended Juzheng and was transferred to judicial administrator of the Lu princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu brought in a doctor to care for Wu's medicine and food, thereby angering Zhang Juzheng, who had him transferred to serve as judicial administrator of the Lu princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 尋假考察罷之。

translations.literal: Soon on the pretext of the review he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was removed on the pretext of the merit review.

sentences.zh: 趙璜，字廷實，安福人。

translations.literal: Zhao Huang, styled Tingshi, was a man of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huang, styled Tingshi, was a native of Anfu.

sentences.zh: 少從父之官，墜江中不死。

translations.literal: In youth he followed his father to his post, fell into the river, and did not die.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he accompanied his father to his posting, fell into a river, and survived.

sentences.zh: 稍長，行道上，得遺金，悉還其主。

translations.literal: When he grew somewhat older, walking on the road he found lost gold and wholly returned it to its owner.
translations.idiomatic: When he was older, he found lost gold on the road and returned all of it to its owner.

sentences.zh: 登弘治三年進士，授工部主事。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the third year of Hongzhi and was appointed a principal in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in Hongzhi 3 and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 改兵部，歷員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of War and served as vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the Ministry of War and rose to vice director.

sentences.zh: 出為濟南知府。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 猾吏舞文，積歲為蠹。

translations.literal: Crafty clerks twisted the statutes and for accumulated years had been a pest.
translations.idiomatic: Crafty clerks had twisted the law for years, becoming a chronic scourge.

sentences.zh: 璜擇願民教之律令，得通習者二十余人，逐吏而代之。

translations.literal: Huang selected willing commoners and taught them statutes; obtaining more than twenty who mastered them, he drove out the clerks and replaced them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huang chose willing locals, trained them in the code, and once he had more than twenty who knew it well, he dismissed the former clerks and put the trained men in their place.

sentences.zh: 漢庶人牧場久籍於官，募民佃。

translations.literal: Pasture lands of the Han commoner estate had long been registered to the government; commoners were recruited to tenant them.
translations.idiomatic: Pasturelands of the Han princely establishment had long been on the government rolls; he opened them to tenant farmers.

sentences.zh: 德王府奏乞之，璜勘還之民。

translations.literal: The Prince of De memorialized begging for them; Huang investigated and returned them to the people.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of De petitioned for those lands, Huang investigated and restored them to the tenants.

sentences.zh: 閱七年，政績大著。

translations.literal: After seven years his administrative achievements were greatly notable.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years his record of governance stood out sharply.

sentences.zh: 正德初，擢順天府丞，未上，劉瑾惡璜，坐巡撫朱欽事，逮下詔獄，除名。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde he was promoted vice prefect of Shuntian; before he took up the post, Liu Jin hated Huang and, implicating him in Grand Coordinator Zhu Qin's affair, had him seized and sent to the imperial prison and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengde reign he was promoted to vice prefect of Shuntian, but before he could take up the post Liu Jin, who hated him, had him imprisoned in connection with grand coordinator Zhu Qin's case and stripped of his name from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，復職。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Jin's execution he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 遷右僉都御史，巡撫宣府。

translations.literal: He was promoted Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 尋調山東。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Shandong.

sentences.zh: 河灘地數百里，賦流民墾而除其租。

translations.literal: Several hundred li of river-beach land he assigned to displaced people to reclaim and remitted their rent.
translations.idiomatic: He set several hundred li of river-bank land to be reclaimed by displaced peasants and exempted them from rent.

sentences.zh: 番僧乞征以充齋糧，帝許之，璜力爭得免。

translations.literal: Tibetan monks begged to levy it to fill fasting provisions; the emperor granted it; Huang strove in argument and obtained exemption.
translations.idiomatic: When Buddhist monks from the borderlands sought to levy taxes on that land for ritual provisions, the emperor agreed, but Huang protested until the levy was dropped.

sentences.zh: 曲阜為賊破，闕里林廟在曠野，璜請移縣就闕里，從之。

translations.literal: Qufu was broken by bandits; the Kong grove and temple stood in open wilds; Huang requested moving the county seat to Konglin and it was followed.
translations.idiomatic: After bandits ravaged Qufu, leaving Confucius's grove and temple exposed in open country, Huang petitioned to move the county seat to Konglin; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 擢工部右侍郎，總理河道。

translations.literal: He was promoted Vice Minister of Works and placed in overall charge of the waterways.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Works with general charge of the waterways.

sentences.zh: 以邊警改理畿輔戎備。

translations.literal: On border alarms he was changed to manage the military defenses of the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: When border alarms arose he was reassigned to manage the defenses of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 事定，命振順天諸府譏，還佐部事。

translations.literal: When matters were settled, he was ordered to relieve famine in Shuntian and other prefectures, and returned to assist in ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Once the crisis passed he was ordered to administer famine relief in Shuntian and neighboring prefectures, then returned to assist at the ministry.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，進左侍郎，掌部事。

translations.literal: When the Shizong emperor acceded, he was advanced to Left Vice Minister and held ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Zhao Huang was promoted to Left Vice Minister and placed in charge of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 裁宦官賜葬費及禦用監料價，革內府酒醋面局歲征鐵磚價銀歲巨萬。

translations.literal: He cut eunuchs' granted burial expenses and material prices of the Directorate of Imperial Use, abolished the inner palace's wine, vinegar, and noodle bureaus' yearly levied iron-brick price silver totaling tens of thousands yearly.
translations.idiomatic: He slashed eunuchs' funeral allowances and inflated prices at the Directorate of Imperial Use, and abolished the inner palace's annual levies on wine, vinegar, and noodle offices for iron and bricks—amounting to tens of thousands of taels each year.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年進尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing he was advanced to minister.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 1 he was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾創玄明宮，糜財數十萬，瑾死，奸人獻為皇莊。

translations.literal: Liu Jin created the Xuansming Palace, wasting funds in the hundreds of thousands; when Jin died, villains presented it as an imperial estate.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin had built Xuansming Palace at a cost of hundreds of thousands; after his death, schemers offered it up as an imperial estate.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，斥以予民，既而中旨令仍舊。

translations.literal: When the emperor acceded, he cast it out to give to the people; afterward an inner edict ordered the former state continued.
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor ordered it returned to the people, but soon a palace edict reversed that and restored the old arrangement.

sentences.zh: 璜言，詔下數月而忽更，示天下不信。

translations.literal: Huang said: an edict issued and within months suddenly changed shows the realm untrustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huang argued that to issue an edict and overturn it within months would show the world that the throne could not be trusted.

sentences.zh: 帝即報許。

translations.literal: The emperor at once replied granting assent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately agreed.

sentences.zh: 會方修仁壽、清寧宮，費不繼。

translations.literal: It happened that they were just then repairing Renshou and Qingning Palaces and funds did not suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Work was under way on Renshou and Qingning Palaces, and funds were running short.

sentences.zh: 璜因請與石景山諸房舍並斥賣以資用，可無累民，帝可之。

translations.literal: Huang therefore requested that together with Shijingshan and various houses they all be sold off to fund use, so the people need not be burdened; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huang therefore proposed selling those holdings along with buildings at Shijingshan to supply the works, sparing the burden on the people; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 給事中徐景嵩等謂，詔書許還民，官不當自鬻，劾璜。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Xu Jingsong and others said: the edict promised return to the people—the office ought not sell on its own; they impeached Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries led by Xu Jingsong argued that since the edict had promised the land to the people, officials had no right to sell it themselves, and they impeached Zhao Huang.

sentences.zh: 璜疏辨，並發景嵩他事。

translations.literal: Huang memorialized in defense and also exposed other matters of Jingsong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huang answered in a memorial, and also brought forward other accusations against Xu Jingsong.

sentences.zh: 御史張鵬翰言璜摭言官，無大臣誼。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Penghan said Huang picked up censorial officials, lacking a grand minister's propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Penghan charged that Zhao Huang was hounding the remonstrating officials and had lost all sense of a senior minister's duty.

sentences.zh: 帝責鵬翰黨庇景嵩，竟斥。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Penghan for factionally protecting Jingsong and in the end dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor upbraided Zhang Penghan for shielding Xu Jingsong and dismissed him in the end.

sentences.zh: 其同官陳江亦以劾璜被責，求去。

translations.literal: His colleague Chen Jiang also, for impeaching Huang, was rebuked and sought to leave.
translations.idiomatic: His colleague Chen Jiang, who had joined the impeachment, was also censured and asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 給事中章僑言璜一舉逐兩諫官，甚損國體。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Zhang Qiao said Huang in one move drove out two remonstrating officials, greatly harming the state's dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Zhang Qiao protested that by one stroke Zhao Huang had driven out two remonstrating officials, gravely damaging the dignity of the court.

sentences.zh: 尚書彭澤復奏僑非是，僑再辨，帝兩解之。

translations.literal: Minister Peng Ze again memorialized that Qiao was wrong; Qiao defended again; the emperor reconciled both.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Peng Ze memorialized that Zhang Qiao was in the wrong; Zhang Qiao replied in his own defense; the emperor smoothed matters over on both sides.

sentences.zh: 詔營後父陳萬言第，估工值六十萬，璜持之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered building the residence of the empress's father Chen Wanyan; estimated construction costs six hundred thousand; Huang held firm on it.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered construction of Empress Chen's father Chen Wanyan's mansion at an estimated cost of six hundred thousand taels, Zhao Huang held the line.

sentences.zh: 萬言訴於帝，下郎中、員外二人詔獄。

translations.literal: Wanyan complained to the emperor; two bureau directors and vice directors were sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wanyan complained to the emperor, who had two division directors thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 璜言：「二臣無與，乞罪臣。」

translations.literal: Huang said: "The two officials had no part in it; I beg punishment for me."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huang wrote: "Those two officials had no part in this; punish me alone."

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 其後論救踵至，萬言不自安，再請貸。

translations.literal: Afterward petitions for rescue arrived in succession; Wanyan was not at ease and again begged leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials pleading for the imprisoned men flooded in; Chen Wanyan, unsettled, again asked that they be spared.

sentences.zh: 二人獲釋，工價亦大減。

translations.literal: The two men obtained release; construction costs also were greatly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The two officials were released, and the construction budget was sharply cut.

sentences.zh: 三年，顯陵司香內官言陵制陜小，請改營，視天壽山諸陵。

translations.literal: In the third year, an inner-palace attendant tending incense at Xianling said the tomb's form was narrow and small, requesting redesign on the model of the tombs at Tianshou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, a eunuch custodian at Xianling reported that the tomb's scale was too small and asked that it be rebuilt to match the Tianshou Mountain mausoleums.

sentences.zh: 璜言陵制與山水相稱，難概同，帝納其言。

translations.literal: Huang said tomb form should match mountains and waters; hard to make uniformly the same; the emperor accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huang replied that a tomb's design should suit its terrain and could not simply be copied; the emperor accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 已，帝欲遷顯陵，璜不可，乃寢。

translations.literal: Already afterward the emperor wished to relocate Xianling; Huang refused; then it was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor proposed moving Xianling altogether; Zhao Huang objected, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 詔建玉德殿，景福、安喜二宮，璜請俟仁壽宮成，徐議其事，帝不許。

translations.literal: An edict ordered building Yude Hall and the two palaces Jingfu and Anxi; Huang asked to wait until Renshou Palace was completed and then slowly discuss the matter; the emperor did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: When orders came to build Yude Hall and the Jingfu and Anxi palaces, Zhao Huang asked to defer discussion until Renshou Palace was finished; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以災異申前請，帝始從之，並罷仁壽役。

translations.literal: Shortly after, on calamities and anomalies he renewed the prior request; the emperor then followed it and also halted Renshou labors.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, citing portents and disasters, he renewed his earlier plea; the emperor relented and also suspended work on Renshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 江西建真人府，陜西督織造，皆遣中使，璜皆疏爭。

translations.literal: Jiangxi built a Perfected One's residence; Shaanxi supervised textile manufacture—all dispatched inner eunuchs; Huang on each memorialized in contention.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangxi was ordered to build a palace for a Taoist "Perfected One" and Shaanxi to oversee imperial silk works, both missions were placed under palace eunuchs; Zhao Huang protested each time by memorial.

sentences.zh: 營建世廟，中官所派物料，戶部多裁省。

translations.literal: Building the lineage temple, materials dispatched by inner eunuchs, the Ministry of Revenue mostly cut and saved.
translations.idiomatic: During construction of the dynastic temple, the Ministry of Revenue pared back much of what the palace eunuchs requisitioned.

sentences.zh: 帝以問璜，璜言曩造乾清、坤寧兩宮所積余貲，足移用，帝遂報可。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Huang; Huang said formerly in building the Qianqing and Kunning palaces surplus funds accumulated, sufficient to transfer use; the emperor then replied approval.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked his view, Zhao Huang said surplus funds from earlier work on the Qianqing and Kunning palaces would suffice; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 璜為尚書六年，值帝初政，銳意厘剔，中官不敢撓，故得舉其職。

translations.literal: Huang served as minister six years; it met the emperor's early rule, keen to reform and purge; inner eunuchs did not dare obstruct; therefore he could fulfill his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huang served six years as minister during the emperor's early reign, when reform was pursued vigorously and palace eunuchs dared not interfere, so he was able to perform his office.

sentences.zh: 後論執不已，諸權幸嫉者眾，帝意亦浸疏。

translations.literal: Later his arguments persisted without cease; many favored and jealous people were numerous; the emperor's regard also gradually grew distant.
translations.idiomatic: But as he continued to remonstrate without letup, he made enemies among the powerful, and the emperor's favor slowly cooled.

sentences.zh: 璜素與秦金齊名。

translations.literal: Huang had long been famed alongside Qin Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huang had long stood equal in reputation with Qin Jin.

sentences.zh: 考察自陳，與金俱致仕。

translations.literal: On the review each petitioned himself; with Jin both retired.
translations.idiomatic: At the merit review both submitted their retirements and left office together.

sentences.zh: 廷臣乞留，不許，馳驛給夫廩如故事。

translations.literal: Court ministers begged to retain them; not permitted; post-horses with bearers and stipends according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The court pleaded to keep them, but the emperor refused; they were sent home with post-horses, bearers, and grain allowance as custom prescribed.

sentences.zh: 璜有幹局，多智慮。

translations.literal: Huang had capacity for affairs and much forethought.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huang had a gift for administration and no lack of shrewd judgment.

sentences.zh: 事棼錯，他人相顧愕眙，璜立辦。

translations.literal: When affairs were tangled in confusion, others looked at one another stunned; Huang at once handled it.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs were in chaos and others stood staring, Zhao Huang set them straight at once.

sentences.zh: 既去，人爭薦之。

translations.literal: Once he had gone, people competed in recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: After he retired, officials vied to recommend him for recall.

sentences.zh: 十一年召復故官，未上卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year summoned to restore his former office; before he reported he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was summoned back to his old post but died before he could take it up.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚莊靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and posthumous name Zhuangjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Zhuangjing, "Stern and Tranquil."

sentences.zh: 鄒文盛，字時鳴，公安人。

translations.literal: Zou Wensheng, styled Shiming, was a man of Gong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Wensheng, styled Shiming, was a native of Gong'an.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the sixth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Hongzhi 6.

sentences.zh: 除吏科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel.

sentences.zh: 遼東巡撫韓重劾鎮守中官廖玘，文盛偕郎中楊茂仁勘實其罪，謫長陵司香。

translations.literal: Liaodong grand coordinator Han Chong impeached the garrison eunuch Liao Chi; Wensheng together with bureau director Yang Maoren verified his crimes; he was demoted to tend incense at Changling.
translations.idiomatic: When Liaodong grand coordinator Han Chong impeached the garrison eunuch Liao Chi, Zou Wensheng and bureau director Yang Maoren investigated and confirmed the charges; Liao was demoted to tend incense at Changling.

sentences.zh: 雜顏三衛屢擾邊，文盛還奏制馭六策。

translations.literal: The Zayan Three Guards repeatedly harassed the border; Wensheng on return memorialized six policies for control.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zayan Three Guards raided the frontier repeatedly, Zou Wensheng memorialized six measures for controlling them.

sentences.zh: 尚書劉大夏深善之，下之邊吏。

translations.literal: Minister Liu Daxia deeply approved them and sent them down to border officials.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Liu Daxia strongly approved and circulated them to frontier officials.

sentences.zh: 尋出核兩廣糧儲。

translations.literal: Soon he went out to audit grain stores of the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon dispatched to audit grain reserves in the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 思恩土官岑濬與田州岑猛構兵，文盛言：「田州廣西之藩蔽，李蠻田州之幹城，參政武清受濬重賂，以計殺蠻釀成禍亂。

translations.literal: The native official Cen Jun of Si'en and Cen Meng of Tianzhou raised arms against each other; Wensheng said: "Tianzhou is Guangxi's outer shield; Li Man is Tianzhou's mainstay; Vice Commissioner Wu Qing accepted Jun's heavy bribes and by stratagem killed Man, brewing calamity and chaos.
translations.idiomatic: When the native official Cen Jun of Si'en and Cen Meng of Tianzhou went to war, Zou Wensheng wrote: "Tianzhou is Guangxi's outer bulwark; Li Man is Tianzhou's pillar of defense. Vice commissioner Wu Qing accepted heavy bribes from Cen Jun and contrived Li Man's death, setting disaster in motion.

sentences.zh: 制敕房供事參議岑業，濬懿親，為彌縫於中，漏我機事。

translations.literal: Cen Ye, associate administrator on duty in the Edicts Chancery, Jun's close kinsman, smoothed over matters within and leaked our operational secrets.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Ye of the Edicts Chancery—a close kinsman of Cen Jun—papered over the affair from inside the court and leaked our plans.

sentences.zh: 請先誅二人，而後行討。」

translations.literal: I request first executing the two men, and afterward proceeding with the punitive campaign."
translations.idiomatic: Execute these two men first, then proceed with the punitive campaign."

sentences.zh: 業有內援，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Ye had inner backing; the emperor did not heed.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Ye had protectors at court, and the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 清尋以考察罷。

translations.literal: Qing soon on the review was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Qing was soon removed in the merit review.

sentences.zh: 正德初，歷戶科都給事中，出為保定知府，累遷福建左布政使。

translations.literal: Early Zhengde, he served through Chief Supervising Secretary in the Revenue Office, went out as prefect of Baoding, and by stages was moved to Left Provincial Administrator of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengde reign he rose to chief supervising secretary in the revenue office, then served as prefect of Baoding and eventually as left provincial administrator of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 十一年以右副都御史巡撫貴州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he grand-coordinated Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 清平苗阿旁、阿階、阿革稱王，巡撫曹祥調永順、保靖土兵討之，尋被劾罷。

translations.literal: Qingping Miao Apang, Ajie, and Age proclaimed themselves kings; grand coordinator Cao Xiang mobilized Yongshun and Baojing native troops to punish them; soon he was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Apang, Ajie, and Age of the Qingping Miao declared themselves kings; grand coordinator Cao Xiang mustered native troops from Yongshun and Baojing to suppress them, but was soon impeached and removed.

sentences.zh: 阿旁等據香爐山，興隆、偏橋、平越、新添、龍裏諸衛鹹被其患。

translations.literal: Apang and others held Mount Xianglu; the guards Xinglong, Pianqiao, Pingyue, Xintian, Longli, and others were all afflicted by their harm.
translations.idiomatic: Apang and his followers held Mount Xianglu, and the guard posts of Xinglong, Pianqiao, Pingyue, Xintian, Longli, and others all suffered from their raids.

sentences.zh: 文盛至，檄川、湖兵協剿，以貴州兵搗炮木寨，擒阿革。

translations.literal: When Wensheng arrived, he issued orders for Sichuan and Huguang troops to join the campaign, sent Guizhou forces to strike Paomu Stockade, and captured Age.
translations.idiomatic: When Zou Wensheng arrived, he mobilized troops from Sichuan and Huguang for a joint campaign and sent Guizhou forces to storm Paomu Stockade, capturing Age.

sentences.zh: 川、湖兵至，抵山下。

translations.literal: The Sichuan and Huguang troops arrived and reached the foot of the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The Sichuan and Huguang troops arrived and encamped at the foot of the mountain.

sentences.zh: 山壁立，惟小徑五，賊皆樹柵。

translations.literal: The mountain rose sheer; there were only five narrow paths, and the rebels had palisades all along them.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain rose sheer from the ground; only five narrow paths led upward, and the rebels had palisades posted on every one.

sentences.zh: 仰攻不能克，乃制戰樓與崖齊，乘夜雨附崖登，拔柵焚廬舍。

translations.literal: Assault from below failed, so they built siege towers level with the cliffs and, under cover of a night rain, scaled the rock face, tore down the palisades, and burned the huts.
translations.idiomatic: Assault from below failed, so they built siege towers level with the cliffs and, under cover of a night rain, scaled the rock face, tore down the palisades, and burned the rebels' huts.

sentences.zh: 賊奔後山，據絕頂。

translations.literal: The rebels fled to the rear slopes and held the summit.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled to the rear slopes and held the summit.

sentences.zh: 官軍乘間梯藤木以上，遂擒阿旁，余賊盡平。

translations.literal: Government troops seized an opening, climbing on vines and timber, captured Apang, and pacified the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops seized an opening, climbing on vines and timber, captured Apang, and pacified the remaining rebels.

sentences.zh: 移師討平龍頭、都黎、都蘭、都蓬、密西、大支、馬羅諸寨黑苗，先後斬降無算。

translations.literal: They then marched against Black Miao stockades at Longtou, Duli, Dulan, Dupeng, Mixi, Dazhi, Maluo, and others, killing and accepting surrender in numbers beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: They then marched against Black Miao stockades at Longtou, Duli, Dulan, Dupeng, Mixi, Dazhi, Maluo, and others, killing and accepting surrender in numbers beyond count.

sentences.zh: 錄功，增俸一等，蔭子錦衣世百戶。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded: one grade added to his salary, and hereditary enrollment of his son as a hundred-household officer in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was recorded: his salary was raised one grade, and his son was granted hereditary enrollment as a hundred-household officer in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 力辭免。

translations.literal: He pressed hard to decline both honors.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed hard to decline both honors.

sentences.zh: 芒部陳聰等為亂，討破之。

translations.literal: When Chen Cong of Mangbu and others rose in revolt, he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Cong of Mangbu and others rose in revolt, he defeated them.

sentences.zh: 四川土舍重安馮綸與凱裏楊弘有怨。

translations.literal: Feng Lun, a native officer of Chong'an in Sichuan, bore a grudge against Yang Hong of Kaili.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Lun, a native officer of Chong'an in Sichuan, bore a grudge against Yang Hong of Kaili.

sentences.zh: 弘卒，綸糾諸苗相仇殺，侵軼貴州境。

translations.literal: After Hong died, Lun incited various Miao groups to mutual slaughter and raided into Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Hong died, Feng Lun incited various Miao groups to mutual slaughter and raided into Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 文盛遣參議蔡潮詣播州，督宣慰楊斌撫定之。

translations.literal: Wensheng dispatched vice commissioner Cai Chao to Bozhou to supervise pacification commissioner Yang Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Wensheng dispatched vice commissioner Cai Chao to Bozhou to supervise pacification commissioner Yang Bin in restoring order.

sentences.zh: 請復設安寧宣撫司，以弘子襲，而錄潮功。

translations.literal: He petitioned to restore the Anning Pacification Commission, let Hong's son succeed, and credit Cai Chao.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to restore the Anning Pacification Commission, let Hong's son succeed, and record Cai Chao's merit.

sentences.zh: 尚書王瓊以專擅為潮罪，不敘。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Qiong punished Cai Chao for overstepping authority and denied him merit credit.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Qiong punished Cai Chao for acting on his own authority and denied him merit credit.

sentences.zh: 頃之，改蒞南京都察院。

translations.literal: Shortly after, he was transferred to the Nanjing Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was transferred to the Nanjing Censorate.

sentences.zh: 梁材，字大用，南京金吾右衛人。

translations.literal: Liang Cai, styled Dayong, was from the Right Jinwu Guard in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Cai, styled Dayong, was a native of the Right Jinwu Guard in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Hongzhi 12.

sentences.zh: 授德清知縣，勤敏有異政。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Deqing, where his diligence and quick competence produced outstanding governance.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed magistrate of Deqing, where his diligence and quick competence produced outstanding governance.

sentences.zh: 正德初，遷刑部主事，改御史。

translations.literal: Early in Zhengde, promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of Justice, then made a censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengde reign he was promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of Justice, then made a censor.

sentences.zh: 出為嘉興知府，調杭州。

translations.literal: Sent out as prefect of Jiaxing, then transferred to Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Jiaxing, then transferred to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 田租例參差，材為酌輕重，立畫一之法。

translations.literal: Land rents varied wildly by custom; Cai weighed heavy and light cases and established a uniform method.
translations.idiomatic: Land rents varied wildly by custom; Liang Cai weighed heavy and light cases and established a uniform method.

sentences.zh: 遷浙江右參政，進按察使。

translations.literal: Promoted to Right Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang, then to provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang, then to provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鎮守中官畢真與宸濠通，將舉城應之。

translations.literal: Garrison eunuch Bi Zhen colluded with Prince Ning and planned to raise the city in his support.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison eunuch Bi Zhen colluded with Prince Ning and planned to raise the city in his support.

sentences.zh: 材與巡按張縉劫持真，奪其兵衛。

translations.literal: Cai and touring inspector Zhang Jin seized Bi Zhen and stripped him of his guard.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Cai and touring inspector Zhang Jin seized Bi Zhen and stripped him of his guard.

sentences.zh: 尋以憂去。

translations.literal: Soon after he left office to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: He soon left office to mourn.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，起補雲南。

translations.literal: Early in Jiajing, recalled to serve in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign he was recalled to serve in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 土官相仇殺累年，材召其酋曰：「汝罪當死。
