translations.literal: Native chiefs had feuded for years; Cai summoned them and said: "Your crimes merit death.
translations.idiomatic: Native chiefs had feuded for years; Liang Cai summoned them and said: "Your crimes merit death.

sentences.zh: 今貰汝，以牛羊贖。」

translations.literal: Today I spare you; redeem yourselves with cattle and sheep."
translations.idiomatic: Today I spare you; redeem yourselves with cattle and sheep."

sentences.zh: 御史訝其輕，材曰：「如是足矣，急之變生。」

translations.literal: A censor found the penalty too light; Cai said: "This is enough; push too hard and rebellion follows."
translations.idiomatic: A censor found the penalty too light; Liang Cai said: "This is enough; push too hard and rebellion follows."

sentences.zh: 諸酋衷甲待變，聞無他乃止。

translations.literal: The chiefs had worn armor beneath their robes awaiting trouble, but hearing nothing further, they stood down.
translations.idiomatic: The chiefs had worn armor beneath their robes awaiting trouble, but hearing nothing further, they stood down.

sentences.zh: 歷貴州、廣東左、右布政使。

translations.literal: He served in turn as left and right provincial administrator of Guizhou and Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as left and right provincial administrator of Guizhou and Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 吏民輸課，令自操權衡，吏不得預。

translations.literal: For tax payments by officials and commoners alike, he required them to operate the scales themselves, with no clerk intervention.
translations.idiomatic: For tax payments by officials and commoners alike, he required them to operate the scales themselves, with no clerk intervention.

sentences.zh: 時天下布政使廉名最著者二人，材與姚鏌也。

translations.literal: At the time the two provincial administrators most renowned for integrity were Cai and Yao Mo.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the two provincial administrators most renowned for integrity were Liang Cai and Yao Mo.

sentences.zh: 六年拜右副都御史，巡撫江西。

translations.literal: In the sixth year appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 甫兩月，召為刑部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Barely two months later summoned as Left Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Barely two months later he was summoned as Left Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 尋改戶部，遂代鄒文盛為尚書。

translations.literal: Soon moved to the Ministry of Revenue and replaced Zou Wensheng as minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to the Ministry of Revenue and replaced Zou Wensheng as minister.

sentences.zh: 自外僚登六卿，不滿二載。

translations.literal: From provincial service to one of the Six Ministries in less than two years.
translations.idiomatic: From provincial service to one of the Six Ministries in less than two years.

sentences.zh: 自以受恩深，益盡職。

translations.literal: Mindful of deep imperial favor, he redoubled his diligence.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of deep imperial favor, he redoubled his diligence.

sentences.zh: 上言：「臣考去年所入止百三十萬兩，而所出至二百四十萬。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "My review shows last year's intake at only 1.3 million taels while outlays reached 2.4 million.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "My review shows last year's intake at only 1.3 million taels while outlays reached 2.4 million.

sentences.zh: 加催征不前，邊費無節，兇荒又多奏免，國計安所辦？

translations.literal: Extra levies still fall short, frontier costs know no limit, and famine districts win repeated remissions—how is the state budget to be managed?
translations.idiomatic: Extra levies still fall short, frontier costs know no limit, and famine districts win repeated remissions—how is the state budget to be managed?

sentences.zh: 詳求弊端：一宗藩，二武職，三冗食，四冗費，五逋負。

translations.literal: He identified five abuses in detail: princely establishments, military offices, redundant stipendaries, wasteful spending, and tax arrears.
translations.idiomatic: He identified five abuses in detail: princely establishments, military offices, redundant stipendaries, wasteful spending, and tax arrears.

sentences.zh: 乞集廷臣計畫條請。」

translations.literal: He asked the court to convene ministers, devise plans, and submit them item by item."
translations.idiomatic: He asked the court to convene ministers, devise plans, and submit them item by item."

sentences.zh: 於是宗藩、武職各議上三事，其他皆嚴為節。

translations.literal: Princely and military offices each proposed three measures; everything else was strictly curtailed.
translations.idiomatic: Princely and military offices each proposed three measures; everything else was strictly curtailed.

sentences.zh: 帝悉報可。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of it.

sentences.zh: 惟武職閑住者議停半俸，帝不納。

translations.literal: Only the proposal to halve stipends for idle military officers was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Only the proposal to halve stipends for idle military officers was rejected.

sentences.zh: 經費大省，國用亦充。

translations.literal: Expenditures dropped sharply and the treasury was replenished.
translations.idiomatic: Expenditures dropped sharply and the treasury was replenished.

sentences.zh: 中官麥福請盡征牧馬草場租，材不可。

translations.literal: Eunuch Mai Fu asked to collect all pasture rents in full; Cai refused.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Mai Fu asked to collect all pasture rents in full; Liang Cai refused.

sentences.zh: 侍郎王軏清勛戚莊田，言宜量等級為限。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Wang Yue audited noble and consort kin estates and said limits should vary by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Wang Yue audited noble and consort kin estates and said limits should vary by rank.

sentences.zh: 材奏：「成周班祿有土田，祿由田出，非常祿外復有土田。

translations.literal: Cai memorialized: "Under the Zhou, ranked stipends included land; income came from land, not regular stipends plus extra estates.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Cai memorialized: "Under the Zhou, ranked stipends included land; income came from land, not regular stipends plus extra estates.

sentences.zh: 今勛戚祿已逾分，而陳乞動千萬，請申禁之。

translations.literal: Now noble stipends already exceed proper measure, yet petitions routinely seek millions—I beg a strict ban.
translations.idiomatic: Now noble stipends already exceed proper measure, yet petitions routinely seek millions—I beg a strict ban.

sentences.zh: 自特賜外，量存三之一，以供祀事。」

translations.literal: Beyond special grants, retain only one-third for sacrificial obligations."
translations.idiomatic: Beyond special grants, retain only one-third for sacrificial obligations."

sentences.zh: 帝命並清已賜者，額外侵據悉還之民，勢豪家乃不敢妄請乞。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered all prior grants reviewed; illegal encroachments were returned to the people, and the powerful dared not petition recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered all prior grants reviewed; illegal encroachments were returned to the people, and the powerful dared not petition recklessly.

sentences.zh: 畿輔屯田，御史督理，正統間易以僉事，權輕，屯政日弛。

translations.literal: Metropolitan garrison farms were overseen by censors; in the Zhengtong era this shifted to assistant commissioners, authority weakened, and farm administration decayed.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan garrison farms were overseen by censors; in the Zhengtong era this shifted to assistant commissioners, authority weakened, and farm administration decayed.

sentences.zh: 材請仍用御史。

translations.literal: Cai asked to restore censor supervision.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Cai asked to restore censor supervision.

sentences.zh: 御史郭弘化言天下土田視國初減半，宜通行清丈。

translations.literal: Censor Guo Honghua said land nationwide had halved since the founding and called for universal remeasurement.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Guo Honghua said land nationwide had halved since the founding and called for universal remeasurement.

sentences.zh: 材恐紛擾，請但敕所司清厘，籍難稽者始履畝而丈。

translations.literal: Fearing disorder, Cai asked only that offices clarify records and measure acre by acre where registers could not be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing disorder, Liang Cai asked only that offices clarify records and measure acre by acre where registers could not be verified.

sentences.zh: 帝悉可之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved everything.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved everything.

sentences.zh: 母喪去。

translations.literal: He left to mourn his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 服除，起故官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was recalled to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 大同巡撫樊繼祖請益軍餉，材言：「大同歲餉七十七萬有奇，例外解發又累萬，較昔已數倍。

translations.literal: Datong grand coordinator Fan Jizu requested more military funds; Cai said: "Datong already receives over 770,000 taels yearly, plus tens of thousands in special disbursements—several times the old level.
translations.idiomatic: Datong grand coordinator Fan Jizu requested more military funds; Liang Cai said: "Datong already receives over 770,000 taels yearly, plus tens of thousands in special disbursements—several times the old level.

sentences.zh: 日益月增，太倉銀不足供一鎮，無論九邊也。」

translations.literal: Month by month it grows; the Grand Canal treasury cannot supply one garrison, let alone all nine frontiers."
translations.idiomatic: Month by month it grows; the Grand Canal treasury cannot supply one garrison, let alone all nine frontiers."

sentences.zh: 繼祖數請不得，議開事例，下戶、兵二部行之。

translations.literal: Fan's repeated petitions were denied; sale-of-office quotas were opened instead and sent to the Revenue and War ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's repeated petitions were denied; sale-of-office quotas were opened instead and sent to the Revenue and War ministries.

sentences.zh: 時修建兩宮、七陵，役京軍七萬，郭勛請給月糧冬衣。

translations.literal: While two palaces and seven tombs were under construction using 70,000 capital troops, Guo Xun requested monthly grain and winter clothing.
translations.idiomatic: While two palaces and seven tombs were under construction using 70,000 capital troops, Guo Xun requested monthly grain and winter clothing.

sentences.zh: 材言非故事，如所請，當歲費銀四十五萬；

translations.literal: Cai said this broke precedent; if granted, it would cost 450,000 taels that year;
translations.idiomatic: Liang Cai said this broke precedent; if granted, it would cost 450,000 taels that year;

sentences.zh: 且冬衣例取內庫，非部事。

translations.literal: and winter clothing customarily came from the inner treasury, not his ministry.
translations.idiomatic: and winter clothing customarily came from the inner treasury, not his ministry.

sentences.zh: 勛怒，劾材誤公。

translations.literal: Guo Xun, enraged, impeached Cai for obstructing state business.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xun, enraged, impeached Liang Cai for obstructing state business.

sentences.zh: 帝詰責材，竟如勛奏。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Cai and sided with Guo Xun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Liang Cai and sided with Guo Xun.

sentences.zh: 勛復建言三事：請開礦助工，余鹽盡輸邊，漕卒得攜貨物。

translations.literal: Guo Xun proposed three more measures: open mines to fund construction, send surplus salt revenue to the frontier, and let transport grain crews carry cargo.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xun proposed three more measures: open mines to fund construction, send surplus salt revenue to the frontier, and let transport grain crews carry cargo.

sentences.zh: 材議，不盡行，勛益怒。

translations.literal: Cai's review let only part pass; Guo Xun grew angrier still.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Cai's review let only part pass; Guo Xun grew angrier still.

sentences.zh: 材初為戶部，值帝勤政，力祛宿弊，多見從。

translations.literal: When Cai first took the Revenue ministry, the diligent emperor backed his purge of longstanding abuses.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Cai first took the Revenue ministry, the diligent emperor backed his purge of longstanding abuses.

sentences.zh: 及是屢忤權幸，不得誌，乃乞改南。

translations.literal: But repeated clashes with favorites frustrated him, and he asked transfer to the south.
translations.idiomatic: But repeated clashes with favorites frustrated him, and he asked to transfer to the south.

sentences.zh: 為給事中周充所劾，下吏部，尚書許贊等請留之。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Zhou Chong impeached him; the case went to the Ministry of Personnel, where Minister Xu Zan and others asked to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Zhou Chong impeached him; the case went to the Ministry of Personnel, where Minister Xu Zan and others asked to keep him.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，令與材俱對狀。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and ordered both men to answer charges in person.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and ordered both men to answer charges in person.

sentences.zh: 材引罪得宥，而贊等坐奪俸。

translations.literal: Cai accepted blame and was spared; Xu Zan and others lost salary as punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Cai accepted blame and was spared; Xu Zan and others lost salary as punishment.

sentences.zh: 材由此失帝意。

translations.literal: From this Cai lost imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: From this Liang Cai lost imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 考尚書六年滿，遂令致仕。

translations.literal: When his six-year term expired, he was ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: When his six-year term as minister expired, he was ordered to retire.

sentences.zh: 初，徽王守莊者與佃人訟，材請革守莊者，令有司納租於王，報可。

translations.literal: Earlier the Prince of Huai's estate managers had sued tenants; Cai proposed abolishing managers and having officials pay rents directly to the prince, which was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Prince of Huai's estate managers had sued tenants; Liang Cai proposed abolishing managers and having officials pay rents directly to the prince, which was approved.

sentences.zh: 王奏不便，帝又從之。

translations.literal: The prince complained of hardship and the emperor reversed course.
translations.idiomatic: The prince complained of hardship and the emperor reversed course.

sentences.zh: 材已去，侍郎唐胄等執初詔。

translations.literal: Cai had already left when Vice Minister Tang Zhou and others held to the original edict.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Cai had already left when Vice Minister Tang Zhou and others held to the original edict.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，並責材。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious and blamed Cai as well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and blamed Liang Cai as well.

sentences.zh: 令以右侍郎閑住，而奪胄俸，下郎官詔獄。

translations.literal: Cai was sidelined as idle Right Vice Minister; Tang Zhou lost salary and a division director went to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Cai was sidelined as idle Right Vice Minister; Tang Zhou lost salary and a division director went to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 明年，戶部尚書李廷相罷。

translations.literal: The next year Revenue Minister Li Tingxiang was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Revenue Minister Li Tingxiang was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 帝念材廉勤，大臣亦多薦者，乃召復故官，加太子少保。

translations.literal: Remembering Cai's integrity and diligence amid many recommendations, the emperor recalled him and made him Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering Liang Cai's integrity and diligence amid many recommendations, the emperor recalled him and made him Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 三掌國計，砥節守公如一日，帝眷亦甚厚。

translations.literal: Three times he held the national accounts, scrupulous as ever, and imperial regard ran deep.
translations.idiomatic: Three times he held the national accounts, scrupulous as ever, and imperial regard ran deep.

sentences.zh: 其秋，考察京官，特命監之。

translations.literal: That autumn he was specially ordered to supervise the capital officials' merit review.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was specially ordered to supervise the capital officials' merit review.

sentences.zh: 有大獄不能決，又命兼掌刑部事。

translations.literal: When a major case could not be settled, he was also put in charge of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When a major case could not be settled, he was also put in charge of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 帝嘆曰：「尚書得如材者十二人，吾無憂天下矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed: "Twelve ministers like Cai, and I would have no worry for the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed: "Twelve ministers like Liang Cai, and I would have no worry for the realm."

sentences.zh: 大工頻興，役外衛班軍四萬六千人。

translations.literal: Major construction continued, employing 46,000 garrison rotation troops from outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Major construction continued, employing 46,000 garrison rotation troops from outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 郭勛籍其不至得，責輸銀雇役，廩食視班軍。

translations.literal: Guo Xun seized on absences to demand silver for hired labor and grain equal to capital troops.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xun seized on absences to demand silver for hired labor and grain equal to capital troops.

sentences.zh: 廷相嘗量給之，材堅持不予。

translations.literal: Tingxiang had once granted partial payment; Cai steadfastly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tingxiang had once granted partial payment; Liang Cai steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 勛劾材，帝命補給。

translations.literal: Guo Xun impeached Cai; the emperor ordered payment.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xun impeached Liang Cai; the emperor ordered payment.

sentences.zh: 勛又以軍不足，籍逃亡軍布棉折餉銀募工。

translations.literal: Guo Xun then cited troop shortages and proposed converting deserters' cloth and cotton stipends into silver to hire workers.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xun then cited troop shortages and proposed converting deserters' cloth and cotton stipends into silver to hire workers.

sentences.zh: 材言：「今京班軍四萬余，已足用，不宜借口耗國儲。」

translations.literal: Cai said: "Over 40,000 capital rotation troops suffice; this pretext must not drain the treasury."
translations.idiomatic: Liang Cai said: "Over 40,000 capital rotation troops suffice; this pretext must not drain the treasury."

sentences.zh: 帝從其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his memorial.

sentences.zh: 勛益怒，劾材變亂舊章。

translations.literal: Guo Xun grew angrier still and charged Cai with overturning established rules.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xun grew angrier still and charged Liang Cai with overturning established rules.

sentences.zh: 無是，醮壇須龍涎香，材不以時進，帝銜之。

translations.literal: Apart from that, the altar rites required ambergris incense and Cai failed to deliver it on time; the emperor nursed a grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from that, the altar rites required ambergris incense and Liang Cai failed to deliver it on time; the emperor nursed a grievance.

sentences.zh: 遂責材沽名誤事，落職閑住。

translations.literal: He was then charged with grandstanding at the expense of duty and dismissed to idle status.
translations.idiomatic: He was then charged with grandstanding at the expense of duty and dismissed to idle status.

sentences.zh: 歸，旋卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: He returned home and soon died at seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home and soon died at seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈太子太保，謚端肅。

translations.literal: Early in Longqing he was posthumously given Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and posthumous name Duansu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longqing reign he was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Duansu, "Upright and Solemn."

sentences.zh: 當嘉靖中歲，大臣或阿上取寵，材獨不撓，以是終不容。

translations.literal: During the Jiajing years, many grand ministers flattered the emperor to win favor, but Cai alone would not bend—and for that was never truly tolerated.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing years, many grand ministers flattered the emperor to win favor, but Liang Cai alone would not bend—and for that was never truly tolerated.

sentences.zh: 自材去，邊儲、國用大窘。

translations.literal: After Cai left office, frontier reserves and the state treasury fell into acute distress.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang Cai left office, frontier reserves and the state treasury fell into acute distress.

sentences.zh: 世宗乃嘆曰：「材在，當不至此。」

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor sighed: "If Cai were still in office, it would not have come to this."
translations.idiomatic: The Shizong Emperor sighed: "If Liang Cai were still in office, it would not have come to this."

sentences.zh: 劉麟，字元瑞，本安仁人。

translations.literal: Liu Lin, styled Yuanrui, was a native of Anren.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lin, styled Yuanrui, was a native of Anren.

sentences.zh: 世為南京廣洋衛副千戶，因家焉。

translations.literal: For generations his family had served as assistant battalion commanders in the Nanjing Guangyang Guard, and they settled there.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had served as assistant battalion commanders in the Nanjing Guangyang Guard, and they settled there.

sentences.zh: 績學能文，與顧璘、徐禎卿稱「江東三才子」。

translations.literal: A diligent scholar and able writer, he was called, with Gu Lin and Xu Zhenqing, one of the "Three Talents of the Jiangdong."
translations.idiomatic: A diligent scholar and able writer, he was called, with Gu Lin and Xu Zhenqing, one of the "Three Talents of the Jiangdong."

sentences.zh: 弘治九年成進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of the Hongzhi reign he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Hongzhi reign he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 言官龐泮等下獄，麟偕同年生陸昆抗疏救。

translations.literal: When the remonstrating officials Pang Pan and others were imprisoned, Lin joined his fellow graduate Lu Kun in a joint memorial to save them.
translations.idiomatic: When the remonstrating officials Pang Pan and others were imprisoned, Liu Lin joined his fellow graduate Lu Kun in a joint memorial to save them.

sentences.zh: 除刑部主事，進員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice and promoted to assistant department director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice and promoted to assistant department director.

sentences.zh: 錄囚畿內，平反三百九十余人。

translations.literal: Reviewing prisoners in the capital region, he reversed wrongful convictions for more than three hundred ninety persons.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing prisoners in the capital region, he reversed wrongful convictions for more than three hundred ninety persons.

sentences.zh: 正德初，進郎中，出為紹興府知府。

translations.literal: At the start of the Zhengde reign he was promoted to department director and sent out as prefect of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhengde reign he was promoted to department director and sent out as prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾銜麟不謁謝，甫五月，摭前錄囚細故，罷為民。

translations.literal: Liu Jin resented Lin for failing to call and offer thanks; after only five months he seized on minor matters from the earlier prisoner review and had him reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin resented Liu Lin for failing to call and offer thanks; after only five months he seized on minor matters from the earlier prisoner review and had him reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 士民醵金贐不受，為建小劉祠以配漢劉寵，因寓湖州。

translations.literal: The gentry and people pooled money for his travel expenses, which he refused; they built a Little Liu Shrine in his honor, pairing him with the Han official Liu Chong, and he took up residence in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry and people pooled money for his travel expenses, which he refused; they built a Little Liu Shrine in his honor, pairing him with the Han official Liu Chong, and he took up residence in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 與吳琬、施侃、孫一元、龍霓為「湖南五隱」。

translations.literal: With Wu Wan, Shi Kan, Sun Yiyuan, and Long Ni he was known as the "Five Recluses of Hunan."
translations.idiomatic: With Wu Wan, Shi Kan, Sun Yiyuan, and Long Ni he was known as the "Five Recluses of Hunan."

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，起補西安。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed, Lin was recalled to fill the post at Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Jin was executed, Liu Lin was recalled to fill the post at Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 遭父憂，樂吳興山水，奉父柩葬焉，遂居湖州。

translations.literal: When his father died he took mourning leave, delighted in the landscape of Wuxing, buried his father's coffin there, and settled in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he took mourning leave, delighted in the landscape of Wuxing, buried his father's coffin there, and settled in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 起陜西左參政，督糧儲。

translations.literal: He was recalled as left assistant administrator of Shaanxi and put in charge of grain stores.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as left assistant administrator of Shaanxi and put in charge of grain stores.

sentences.zh: 都御史鄧璋督師，議加賦充餉，麟力爭。

translations.literal: When Censor-in-Chief Deng Zhang commanded the army, he proposed raising taxes to fund provisions; Lin argued fiercely against it.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor-in-Chief Deng Zhang commanded the army, he proposed raising taxes to fund provisions; Liu Lin argued fiercely against it.

sentences.zh: 會陜民詣闕訴，得寢。

translations.literal: Soon Shaanxi commoners petitioned at court, and the plan was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shaanxi commoners petitioned at court, and the plan was shelved.

sentences.zh: 尋遷雲南按察使，謝病歸。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to be surveillance commissioner of Yunnan, then retired on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was transferred to be surveillance commissioner of Yunnan, then retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，召拜太仆卿。

translations.literal: At the start of the Jiajing reign he was summoned and appointed Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jiajing reign he was summoned and appointed Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 進右副都御史，巡撫保定六府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of the six prefectures of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of the six prefectures of Baoding.

sentences.zh: 中官耿忠守備紫荊多縱，麟劾奏之。

translations.literal: The eunuch Geng Zhong, defending Zijing Pass, was excessively lax; Lin impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Geng Zhong, defending Zijing Pass, was excessively lax; Liu Lin impeached him.

sentences.zh: 請捐天津三衛屯田課，及出庫儲給河間三衛軍月餉，征逋課以償，皆報可。

translations.literal: He asked to remit the land-tax levies on garrison farms of the three guards at Tianjin and to draw from treasury reserves to pay the monthly stipends of the three guards at Hejian, recovering overdue taxes to make up the cost—all approved.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to remit the land-tax levies on garrison farms of the three guards at Tianjin and to draw from treasury reserves to pay the monthly stipends of the three guards at Hejian, recovering overdue taxes to make up the cost—all approved.

sentences.zh: 帝因諭戶部，中外軍餉未給者，悉補給之。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore instructed the Ministry of Revenue that all military stipends at home and abroad still unpaid should be fully disbursed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore instructed the Ministry of Revenue that all military stipends at home and abroad still unpaid should be fully disbursed.

sentences.zh: 再引疾歸。

translations.literal: He again cited illness and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He again cited illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 起大理卿，拜工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was recalled as President of the Court of Judicial Review and appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as President of the Court of Judicial Review and appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 侍衛軍不給衣履，錦衣帥駱安援紅盔軍例以請，麟執不可。

translations.literal: The palace guard troops were not issued clothing and footwear; the Embroidered Uniform Guard commander Luo An cited the precedent of the Red-Helmet Guard in requesting it, but Lin firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: The palace guard troops were not issued clothing and footwear; the Embroidered Uniform Guard commander Luo An cited the precedent of the Red-Helmet Guard in requesting it, but Liu Lin firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 詔量給銀自制，後五載一給為常。

translations.literal: An edict ordered silver to be measured out for them to make their own, with reissue every five years as the rule.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered silver to be measured out for them to make their own, with reissue every five years as the rule.

sentences.zh: 四司財物悉貯後堂大庫，司官出納多侵漁，麟請特除一郎官主之。

translations.literal: The goods of the four bureaus were all stored in the rear-hall treasury, and bureau officials embezzled much in handling receipts and disbursements; Lin asked that a special clerk be appointed to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: The goods of the four bureaus were all stored in the rear-hall treasury, and bureau officials embezzled much in handling receipts and disbursements; Liu Lin asked that a special clerk be appointed to oversee them.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善，因賜名「節慎庫」。

translations.literal: The emperor praised the plan and bestowed the name "Treasury of Thrift and Care."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the plan and bestowed the name "Treasury of Thrift and Care."

sentences.zh: 已，上節財十四事，汰內府諸監局冒破錢，中貴大恨。

translations.literal: Later he submitted fourteen items on economizing, cutting fraudulent expenditures by the inner-palace directorates and supervisory offices; the eunuch elite deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he submitted fourteen items on economizing, cutting fraudulent expenditures by the inner-palace directorates and supervisory offices; the eunuch elite deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 及顯陵工竣，執役者鹹覬官。

translations.literal: When work on the Xianling Mausoleum was finished, laborers all coveted official posts.
translations.idiomatic: When work on the Xianling Mausoleum was finished, laborers all coveted official posts.

sentences.zh: 麟止擬賚，群小愈怨。

translations.literal: Lin would only recommend modest rewards, and the petty men grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lin would only recommend modest rewards, and the petty men grew still angrier.

sentences.zh: 會帝納諫官言，停中外雜派工役，麟牒停浙江、蘇、松織造，而上供袍服在停中。

translations.literal: When the emperor accepted remonstrating officials' advice and halted miscellaneous labor levies at home and abroad, Lin ordered a halt to weaving in Zhejiang, Suzhou, and Songjiang—including tribute robes for the court among the stoppages.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor accepted remonstrating officials' advice and halted miscellaneous labor levies at home and abroad, Liu Lin ordered a halt to weaving in Zhejiang, Suzhou, and Songjiang—including tribute robes for the court among the stoppages.

sentences.zh: 中官吳勛以為言，遂勒麟致仕。

translations.literal: The eunuch Wu Xun complained, and Lin was forced to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wu Xun complained, and Liu Lin was forced to retire.

sentences.zh: 久之，顯陵殿閣雨漏，追論麟，落職。

translations.literal: Long afterward, when rain leaked through the halls and pavilions of Xianling, Lin was pursued in review and stripped of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward, when rain leaked through the halls and pavilions of Xianling, Liu Lin was pursued in review and stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 麟清修直節，當官不撓。

translations.literal: Lin was pure in conduct and upright in integrity, unyielding in office.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lin was pure in conduct and upright in integrity, unyielding in office.

sentences.zh: 居工部，為朝廷惜財謹費，僅逾年而罷。

translations.literal: At the Ministry of Works he spared the state's wealth and guarded against waste, yet was dismissed after little more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: At the Ministry of Works he spared the state's wealth and guarded against waste, yet was dismissed after little more than a year.

sentences.zh: 居郊外南坦，賦詩自娛。

translations.literal: He lived at Nantan outside the city and amused himself composing poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at Nantan outside the city and amused himself composing poetry.

sentences.zh: 守為築一臺，令為構堂，始有息遊之所。

translations.literal: The prefect built him a terrace and ordered a hall constructed, so that he finally had a place to rest and stroll.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect built him a terrace and ordered a hall constructed, so that he finally had a place to rest and stroll.

sentences.zh: 家居三十余年，廷臣頻論薦。

translations.literal: At home for more than thirty years, court ministers repeatedly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: At home for more than thirty years, court ministers repeatedly recommended him.

sentences.zh: 晚好樓居，力不能構，懸籃輿於梁，曲臥其中，名曰神樓。

translations.literal: In his later years he loved living in an upper story but lacked the strength to build one; he hung a basket-chair from a beam and lay curled within it, calling it the Spirit Tower.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he loved living in an upper story but lacked the strength to build one; he hung a basket-chair from a beam and lay curled within it, calling it the Spirit Tower.

sentences.zh: 文徵明繪圖遺之。

translations.literal: Wen Zhengming painted a picture and sent it to him as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhengming painted a picture and sent it to him as a gift.

sentences.zh: 年八十七卒。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚清惠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Qinghui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Qinghui.

sentences.zh: 蔣瑤，字粹卿，歸安人。

translations.literal: Jiang Yao, styled Cuiqing, was a native of Gui'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yao, styled Cuiqing, was a native of Gui'an.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of the Hongzhi reign he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of the Hongzhi reign he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed an courier.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a courier.

sentences.zh: 正德時，歷兩京御史。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde era he served as censor in both capitals.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengde era he served as censor in both capitals.

sentences.zh: 陳時弊七事，中言：「內府軍器局軍匠六千，中官監督者二人，今增至六十余人，人占軍匠三十。

translations.literal: He set forth seven abuses of the age, saying among them: "The inner-palace Armory Bureau has six thousand military artisans, with two eunuch supervisors; now they have increased to more than sixty, each claiming thirty artisans.
translations.idiomatic: He set forth seven abuses of the age, saying among them: "The inner-palace Armory Bureau has six thousand military artisans, with two eunuch supervisors; now they have increased to more than sixty, each claiming thirty artisans.

sentences.zh: 他局稱是，行伍安得不耗。」

translations.literal: Other bureaus are the same—how can the ranks not be depleted?"
translations.idiomatic: Other bureaus are the same—how can the ranks not be depleted?"

sentences.zh: 並言：「傳奉官及濫收校尉勇士並宜厘革。

translations.literal: He also said: "Commissioned officials and the indiscriminate recruitment of guards, braves, and warriors should all be reformed.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Commissioned officials and the indiscriminate recruitment of guards, braves, and warriors should all be reformed.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾雖誅，權猶在宦豎。」

translations.literal: Though Liu Jin was executed, power still rested with the eunuchs."
translations.idiomatic: Though Liu Jin was executed, power still rested with the eunuchs."

sentences.zh: 有旨詰問，且言「自今如瑤議者，毋復奏。」

translations.literal: An imperial rescript rebuked him and declared that from then on no one should again submit memorials like Yao's."
translations.idiomatic: An imperial rescript rebuked him and declared that from then on no one should again submit memorials like Jiang Yao's."

sentences.zh: 尋出為荊州知府。

translations.literal: He was soon sent out as prefect of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as prefect of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 築黃潭堤。

translations.literal: He built the Huangtan embankment.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Huangtan embankment.

sentences.zh: 調揚州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 武宗南巡至揚，瑤供禦取具而已，無所贈遺。

translations.literal: When the Wuzong Emperor toured south to Yangzhou, Yao supplied only what was needed for the imperial retinue and made no gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuzong Emperor toured south to Yangzhou, Jiang Yao supplied only what was needed for the imperial retinue and made no gifts.

sentences.zh: 諸嬖幸皆怒。

translations.literal: All the favored minions were enraged.
translations.idiomatic: All the favored minions were enraged.

sentences.zh: 江彬欲奪富民居為威武副將軍府，瑤執不可。

translations.literal: Jiang Bin wanted to seize wealthy households' residences for a Vice General of Martial Prestige's mansion; Yao refused.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bin wanted to seize wealthy households' residences for a Vice General of Martial Prestige's mansion; Jiang Yao refused.

sentences.zh: 彬閉瑤空舍挫辱之，脅以帝所賜銅瓜，不為懾。

translations.literal: Bin shut Yao in an empty house to humiliate him and threatened him with the copper mace the emperor had bestowed, but Yao was not intimidated.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bin shut Jiang Yao in an empty house to humiliate him and threatened him with the copper mace the emperor had bestowed, but Jiang Yao was not intimidated.

sentences.zh: 會帝漁獲一巨魚，戲言直五百金，彬即畀瑤責其直。

translations.literal: Once when the emperor caught a huge fish while fishing, he joked that it was worth five hundred taels; Bin immediately handed it to Yao and demanded payment.
translations.idiomatic: Once when the emperor caught a huge fish while fishing, he joked that it was worth five hundred taels; Jiang Bin immediately handed it to Jiang Yao and demanded payment.

sentences.zh: 瑤懷其妻簪珥、袿服以進，曰：「庫無錢，臣所有惟此。」

translations.literal: Yao brought his wife's hairpins, earrings, and formal robes and presented them, saying: "The treasury has no money; all I have is this."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yao brought his wife's hairpins, earrings, and formal robes and presented them, saying: "The treasury has no money; all I have is this."

sentences.zh: 帝笑而遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 府故有瓊花觀，詔取瓊花。

translations.literal: The prefecture had a Qionghua View; an edict ordered the qionghua flower to be presented.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had a Qionghua View; an edict ordered the qionghua flower to be presented.

sentences.zh: 瑤言自宋徽、欽北狩，此花已絕，今無以獻。

translations.literal: Yao said that since the Northern Hunt of the Song emperors Huizong and Qinzong, the flower had been extinct and there was nothing to offer.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yao said that since the Northern Hunt of the Song emperors Huizong and Qinzong, the flower had been extinct and there was nothing to offer.

sentences.zh: 又傳旨征異物，瑤具對非揚產。

translations.literal: When another edict demanded exotic goods, Yao answered in detail that they were not products of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When another edict demanded exotic goods, Jiang Yao answered in detail that they were not products of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「苧白布，亦非揚產耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Ramie white cloth—is that not a Yangzhou product?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Ramie white cloth—is that not a Yangzhou product?"

sentences.zh: 瑤不得已，為獻五百疋。

translations.literal: Yao had no choice and presented five hundred bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yao had no choice and presented five hundred bolts.

sentences.zh: 當是時，權幸以揚繁華，要求無所不至。

translations.literal: At that time the powerful and favored, seeing Yangzhou's wealth, made demands without limit.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the powerful and favored, seeing Yangzhou's wealth, made demands without limit.

sentences.zh: 微瑤，民且重困。

translations.literal: But for Yao, the people would have been doubly burdened.
translations.idiomatic: But for Jiang Yao, the people would have been doubly burdened.

sentences.zh: 駕旋，瑤扈至寶應。

translations.literal: When the imperial procession returned, Yao escorted it as far as Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession returned, Jiang Yao escorted it as far as Baoying.

sentences.zh: 中官邱得用鐵縆系瑤，數日始釋，竟扈至臨清而返。

translations.literal: The eunuch Qiu De bound Yao with iron chains; only after several days was he released, and he escorted the procession all the way to Linqing before returning.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Qiu De bound Jiang Yao with iron chains; only after several days was he released, and he escorted the procession all the way to Linqing before returning.

sentences.zh: 揚人見瑤，無不感泣。

translations.literal: When the people of Yangzhou saw Yao, none failed to weep with gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Yangzhou saw Jiang Yao, none failed to weep with gratitude.

sentences.zh: 迨遷陜西參政，爭出資建祠祀之，名自此大震。

translations.literal: Later, when he was transferred to be assistant administrator of Shaanxi, they vied to contribute funds and build a shrine to worship him; his fame was greatly magnified from then on.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he was transferred to be assistant administrator of Shaanxi, they vied to contribute funds and build a shrine to worship him; his fame was greatly magnified from then on.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，歷湖廣、江西左、右布政使，以右副都御史巡撫河南。

translations.literal: At the start of the Jiajing reign he served successively as left and right provincial administrators of Huguang and Jiangxi, then as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jiajing reign he served successively as left and right provincial administrators of Huguang and Jiangxi, then as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 帝命桂萼等核巡撫官去留，令瑤歸候調。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Gui E and others to review which grand coordinators should stay or go, and directed Yao to return and await reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Gui E and others to review which grand coordinators should stay or go, and directed Jiang Yao to return and await reassignment.

sentences.zh: 已，累遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted step by step to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted step by step to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 四郊工竣，加太子少保。

translations.literal: When work on the four suburban altars was finished, he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When work on the four suburban altars was finished, he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 西苑宮殿成，帝置宴。

translations.literal: When the Western Park palaces were completed, the emperor held a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Park palaces were completed, the emperor held a banquet.

sentences.zh: 見瑤與王時中席在外，命移殿內，而移皇親於殿右以讓瑤，曰：「親親不如尊賢。」

translations.literal: Seeing Yao and Wang Shizhong seated outside, he ordered them moved inside the hall and shifted imperial kinsmen to the right side of the hall to make room for Yao, saying: "Honoring the worthy comes before honoring one's kin."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Jiang Yao and Wang Shizhong seated outside, he ordered them moved inside the hall and shifted imperial kinsmen to the right side of the hall to make room for Jiang Yao, saying: "Honoring the worthy comes before honoring one's kin."

sentences.zh: 其重瑤如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he held Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he held Jiang Yao.

sentences.zh: 時土木繁興，歲費數百萬計。

translations.literal: At the time construction was flourishing, costing millions each year.
translations.idiomatic: At the time construction was flourishing, costing millions each year.

sentences.zh: 瑤規畫鹹稱帝意，數有賚予。

translations.literal: Yao's planning always pleased the emperor, and he received many gifts and grants.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yao's planning always pleased the emperor, and he received many gifts and grants.

sentences.zh: 以憂去。

translations.literal: He left office on mourning leave.
translations.idiomatic: He left office on mourning leave.

sentences.zh: 久之，自南京工部尚書，召改北部。

translations.literal: Long afterward, from Minister of Works at Nanjing he was summoned and transferred to the northern ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward, from Minister of Works at Nanjing he was summoned and transferred to the northern ministry.

sentences.zh: 帝幸承天，瑤扈從。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Chengtian, Yao accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Chengtian, Jiang Yao accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 京師營建，率役京軍，多為豪家占匿。

translations.literal: Capital construction usually conscripted capital troops, many of whom were concealed and kept by powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: Capital construction usually conscripted capital troops, many of whom were concealed and kept by powerful families.

sentences.zh: 至是大工頻仍，歲募民充役，費二百余萬。

translations.literal: Now major works came in rapid succession, and civilians were recruited yearly for corvée at a cost of more than two million taels.
translations.idiomatic: Now major works came in rapid succession, and civilians were recruited yearly for corvée at a cost of more than two million taels.

sentences.zh: 瑤以為言，因請停不急者。

translations.literal: Yao spoke on this and asked that non-urgent projects be halted.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yao spoke on this and asked that non-urgent projects be halted.

sentences.zh: 豪家所匿軍畢出，募直大減。

translations.literal: The troops concealed by powerful families all came forth, and recruitment costs fell sharply.
translations.idiomatic: The troops concealed by powerful families all came forth, and recruitment costs fell sharply.

sentences.zh: 以老致仕去。

translations.literal: He retired on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: He retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 瑤端亮清介。

translations.literal: Yao was upright, bright, and incorruptible.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yao was upright, bright, and incorruptible.

sentences.zh: 既歸，僻處陋巷。

translations.literal: After returning home he lived in a humble lane.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home he lived in a humble lane.

sentences.zh: 與尚書劉麟、顧應祥輩結文酒社，徜徉峴山間。

translations.literal: With the ministers Liu Lin, Gu Yingxiang, and others he formed a literary wine society and wandered among the Xian hills.
translations.idiomatic: With the ministers Liu Lin, Gu Yingxiang, and others he formed a literary wine society and wandered among the Xian hills.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十九。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚恭靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Gongjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Gongjing.

sentences.zh: 王廷相，字子衡，儀封人。

translations.literal: Wang Tingxiang, styled Ziheng, was a native of Yifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingxiang, styled Ziheng, was a native of Yifeng.

sentences.zh: 幼有文名。

translations.literal: From youth he had a literary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had a literary reputation.

sentences.zh: 登弘治十五年進士，選庶吉士，授兵科給事中。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in Hongzhi 15, was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor, and received appointment as a supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Hongzhi 15 (1502), was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor, and received appointment as a supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以憂去。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office on account of mourning.

sentences.zh: 正德初，服闋至京。

translations.literal: Early in the Zhengde reign, when his mourning period ended, he came to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengde reign, when his mourning period ended, he came to the capital.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾中以罪謫亳州判官，量移高淳知縣。

translations.literal: Liu Jin had him demoted for a crime to the post of assistant magistrate of Bozhou; he was then transferred in grade to magistrate of Gaochun.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin had him demoted for a crime to the post of assistant magistrate of Bozhou; he was then transferred in grade to magistrate of Gaochun.

sentences.zh: 召為御史，疏言：「大盜四起，將帥未能平。

translations.literal: He was summoned and made a censor, memorializing: "Great bandits rise on every side, yet commanders cannot pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and made a censor, memorializing: "Great bandits rise on every side, yet commanders cannot pacify them.

sentences.zh: 由將權輕，不能禦敵；

translations.literal: This is because generals have too little authority and cannot resist the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: This is because generals hold too little authority and cannot resist the enemy;

sentences.zh: 兵機疏，不能扼險也。

translations.literal: military plans are lax, and they cannot hold the passes.
translations.idiomatic: military plans are lax, and they cannot hold the strategic passes.

sentences.zh: 盜賊所至，鄉民奉牛酒，甚者為效力。

translations.literal: Wherever bandits go, villagers offer oxen and wine; many even serve them to good effect.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever bandits go, villagers offer oxen and wine; many even serve them willingly.

sentences.zh: 盜有生殺權，而將帥反無之，故兵不用命。

translations.literal: Bandits hold the power of life and death, while commanders in turn do not, so the troops will not obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits hold the power of life and death, while commanders in turn do not, so the troops will not obey orders.

sentences.zh: 宜假便宜，退卻者必斬。

translations.literal: They should be granted discretionary authority: any who retreat must be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders should be granted discretionary authority, with execution mandatory for any who retreat.

sentences.zh: 河南地平曠，賊易奔，山西地險阻，亦縱深入，將帥罪也。

translations.literal: Henan has level, open terrain, so bandits can flee easily; Shanxi has steep, obstructive terrain, yet they are allowed to penetrate deep—in both cases the fault lies with the commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Henan has level, open terrain, so bandits can flee easily; Shanxi has steep, obstructive terrain, yet they are allowed to penetrate deep—in both cases the fault lies with the commanders.

sentences.zh: 若陳兵黃河之津，使不得西，分扼井陘、天井，使不得東，而主將以大軍蹙之，則賊進退皆窮，可不戰擒矣。」

translations.literal: If troops were arrayed at the Yellow River crossings to block the west, and forces stationed to hold Jingxing and Tianjing to block the east, while the chief commander pressed in with a great army, the bandits would be trapped whether they advanced or retreated, and could be captured without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: If troops were arrayed at the Yellow River crossings to block the west, and forces stationed to hold Jingxing and Tianjing to block the east, while the chief commander pressed in with a great army, the bandits would be trapped whether they advanced or retreated and could be captured without fighting."

sentences.zh: 帝切責總督諸臣，悉從其議。

translations.literal: The emperor sharply rebuked the regional governors and fully adopted his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sharply rebuked the regional governors and fully adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 已，出按陜西，裁抑鎮守中官廖堂，被誣。

translations.literal: Before long he went out on an inspection tour of Shaanxi, curtailing the eunuch garrison commander Liao Tang, and was slandered.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he went out on an inspection tour of Shaanxi, curtailing the eunuch garrison commander Liao Tang, and was slandered.

sentences.zh: 時已改督京畿學校，逮系詔獄，謫贛榆丞。

translations.literal: By then he had already been reassigned to oversee capital schools; he was seized and imprisoned in the imperial prison, and demoted to assistant magistrate of Ganyu.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had already been reassigned to oversee capital schools; he was seized and imprisoned in the imperial prison, and demoted to assistant magistrate of Ganyu.

sentences.zh: 屢遷四川僉事，山東副使，皆提督學校。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice commissioner in Sichuan and vice commissioner in Shandong, each time overseeing schools.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to vice commissioner in Sichuan and vice commissioner in Shandong, each time overseeing schools.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年舉治行卓異，再遷山東右布政使。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 2 his administration was cited as outstanding, and he was promoted again to Right Administrator of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 2 (1523) his administration was cited as outstanding, and he was promoted again to Right Administrator of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 以右副都御史巡撫四川，討平芒部賊沙保。

translations.literal: As Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he became governor of Sichuan and suppressed the Mangbu bandit Shabao.
translations.idiomatic: As Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he became governor of Sichuan and suppressed the Mangbu bandit Shabao.

sentences.zh: 尋召理院事。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled to administer the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled to administer the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 歷兵部左、右侍郎，遷南京兵部尚書，參贊機務。

translations.literal: He served successively as Left and Right Vice Minister of War, was transferred to Minister of War at Nanjing, and assisted in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Left and Right Vice Minister of War, was transferred to Minister of War at Nanjing, and assisted in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 初有詔，省進貢快船。

translations.literal: An imperial edict had initially ordered a reduction in tribute express boats.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict had initially ordered a reduction in tribute express boats.

sentences.zh: 守備太監賴義復求增，廷相請酌物輕重以定船數，而大減宣德以後傳旨非祖制者。

translations.literal: The garrison eunuch Lai Yi again requested an increase; Tingxiang asked that the weight of goods be weighed to set the number of boats, and greatly reduced edicts issued after the Xuande reign that were not ancestral institutions.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison eunuch Lai Yi again requested an increase; Wang Tingxiang asked that the weight of goods be weighed to set the number of boats, and greatly reduced edicts issued after the Xuande reign that were not ancestral institutions.

sentences.zh: 龍江、大勝、新江、浦子、江淮五關守臣借稽察榷利，安慶、九江借春秋閱視索賂，廷相皆請革之。

translations.literal: At the five passes of Longjiang, Dasheng, Xinjiang, Puzi, and Jianghuai, local officials used inspection to levy customs profits; at Anqing and Jiujiang they demanded bribes under the pretext of spring and autumn reviews—Tingxiang memorialized to abolish all of this.
translations.idiomatic: At the five passes of Longjiang, Dasheng, Xinjiang, Puzi, and Jianghuai, local officials used inspection to levy customs profits; at Anqing and Jiujiang they demanded bribes under the pretext of spring and autumn reviews—Wang Tingxiang memorialized to abolish all of this.

sentences.zh: 草場、蘆課銀率為中官楊奇、卜春及魏國公徐鵬舉所侵蝕。

translations.literal: Revenues from pasture lands and reed duties were routinely embezzled by the eunuchs Yang Qi and Bu Chun and by Xu Pengju, Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Revenues from pasture lands and reed duties were routinely embezzled by the eunuchs Yang Qi and Bu Chun and by Xu Pengju, Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 以廷相請，逮問奇、春，奪鵬舉祿。

translations.literal: At Tingxiang's request, Qi and Chun were arrested and interrogated, and Pengju's stipend was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: At Wang Tingxiang's request, Qi and Chun were arrested and interrogated, and Pengju's stipend was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 三月入為左都御史，疏言南京守備權太重，不宜令魏國世官。

translations.literal: In the third month he entered office as Left Censor-in-Chief, memorializing that the Nanjing garrison commander's authority was too great and that the Duchy of Wei should not hold the post by hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he entered office as Left Censor-in-Chief, memorializing that the Nanjing garrison commander's authority was too great and that the Duchy of Wei should not hold the post by hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 給事中曾忭亦言之，遂解鵬舉兵柄。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Zeng Bian spoke similarly, and Pengju was thereupon stripped of his military command.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary Zeng Bian spoke similarly, and Pengju was thereupon stripped of his military command.

sentences.zh: 居二年，加兵部尚書兼前官，提督團營，仍理院事。

translations.literal: After two years he was additionally made Minister of War while retaining his previous post, put in charge of the regiment camps, and still administered the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was additionally made Minister of War while retaining his previous post, put in charge of the regiment camps, and still administered the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 兩考滿，加太子少保。

translations.literal: After two terms of appraisal he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After two terms of appraisal he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 畿民盜天壽山陵樹，巡按楊紹芳引盜大祀神禦物，律斬。

translations.literal: A resident of the capital region stole trees from the Tianshou imperial tombs; the touring censor Yang Shaofang applied the statute on stealing sacred vessels for great sacrifices and sentenced him to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: A resident of the capital region stole trees from the Tianshou imperial tombs; the touring censor Yang Shaofang applied the statute on stealing sacred vessels for great sacrifices and sentenced him to decapitation.

sentences.zh: 廷相言：「大祀神禦物者，指神禦在內祭器帷帳之物而言。

translations.literal: Tingxiang said: "The term sacred vessels for great sacrifices refers to the inner ritual implements, curtains, and hangings used in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingxiang said: "The term sacred vessels for great sacrifices refers to the inner ritual implements, curtains, and hangings used in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 律文，盜陵木者，止杖一百，徒三年。

translations.literal: The statute text for stealing tomb timber prescribes only one hundred blows with the rod and three years' penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: The statute text for stealing tomb timber prescribes only one hundred blows with the rod and three years' penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 今舍本律，非刑之平。」

translations.literal: To set aside the primary statute now would not be equitable punishment."
translations.idiomatic: To set aside the primary statute now would not be equitable punishment."

sentences.zh: 忤旨，罰俸一月。

translations.literal: He offended the imperial will and was fined one month's salary.
translations.idiomatic: He offended the imperial will and was fined one month's salary.

sentences.zh: 帝將幸承天，廷相與諸大臣諫，不納。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to visit Chengtian, Tingxiang joined the chief ministers in remonstrance, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to visit Chengtian, Wang Tingxiang joined the chief ministers in remonstrance, but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 扈從還，以九年滿，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Returning from the entourage tour, upon completion of nine years in office he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from the entourage tour, upon completion of nine years in office he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 雷震奉先殿，廷相言：「人事修而後天道順，大臣法而後小臣廉。

translations.literal: Lightning struck the Hall of Imperial Ancestors; Tingxiang said: "Only when human affairs are put in order does the way of Heaven run straight; only when great ministers uphold the law do lesser officials keep themselves pure.
translations.idiomatic: Lightning struck the Hall of Imperial Ancestors; Wang Tingxiang said: "Only when human affairs are put in order does the way of Heaven run straight; only when great ministers uphold the law do lesser officials keep themselves pure.

sentences.zh: 今廉隅不立，賄賂盛行，先朝猶暮夜之私，而今則白日之攫。

translations.literal: Now the corners of integrity are not established and bribery runs rampant; in earlier reigns it was still a matter of secret gifts at night, but now it is brazen plunder in broad daylight.
translations.idiomatic: Now the corners of integrity are not established and bribery runs rampant; in earlier reigns it was still a matter of secret gifts at night, but now it is brazen plunder in broad daylight.

sentences.zh: 大臣汙則小臣悉效，京官貪則外臣無畏。

translations.literal: When great ministers are corrupt, lesser officials all follow suit; when capital officials are greedy, outside officials have nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: When great ministers are corrupt, lesser officials all follow suit; when capital officials are greedy, outside officials have nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 臣職憲紀，不能絕其弊，乞先罷斥。」

translations.literal: In my office of upholding the laws I cannot cut off this abuse; I beg first to be dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: In my office of upholding the laws I cannot cut off this abuse; I beg first to be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 用以刺尚書嚴嵩、張瓚輩。

translations.literal: This was intended as an indirect rebuke of Ministers Yan Song, Zhang Zan, and their like.
translations.idiomatic: This was intended as an indirect rebuke of Ministers Yan Song, Zhang Zan, and their like.

sentences.zh: 帝但諭留而已。

translations.literal: The emperor merely instructed him to remain in office, and that was all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor merely instructed him to remain in office, and that was all.

sentences.zh: 初，廷相請以六條考察差還御史。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tingxiang had asked that censors returning from provincial tours be evaluated according to six criteria.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Tingxiang had asked that censors returning from provincial tours be evaluated according to six criteria.

sentences.zh: 帝令疏其所未盡，編之憲綱。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to set forth what was still incomplete and compile it into the regulations of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to set forth what was still incomplete and compile it into the regulations of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 乃取張孚敬、汪鋐所奏列，及新所定凡十五事以進，悉允行之。

translations.literal: He then took the items memorialized by Zhang Fujing and Wang Hong, together with fifteen newly established provisions, and submitted them; all were approved and put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: He then took the items memorialized by Zhang Fujing and Wang Hong, together with fifteen newly established provisions, and submitted them; all were approved and put into practice.

sentences.zh: 及九廟災，下詔修省，因敕廷相曰：「御史巡方職甚重。

translations.literal: When fire destroyed the Nine Temples, an edict was issued calling for self-examination, and the emperor charged Tingxiang: "The duty of censors touring the provinces is weighty indeed.
translations.idiomatic: When fire destroyed the Nine Temples, an edict was issued calling for self-examination, and the emperor charged Wang Tingxiang: "The duty of censors touring the provinces is weighty indeed.

sentences.zh: 卿總憲有年，自定六條後，不考黜一人，今宜痛修省。」

translations.literal: You have presided over the Censorate for many years, yet since the six criteria were established you have not dismissed a single man through evaluation; you should now earnestly examine yourself."
translations.idiomatic: You have presided over the Censorate for many years, yet since the six criteria were established you have not dismissed a single man through evaluation; you should now earnestly examine yourself."

sentences.zh: 廷相惶恐謝。

translations.literal: Tingxiang, in alarm, apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingxiang, in alarm, apologized.

sentences.zh: 廷相掌內臺最久，有威重。

translations.literal: Tingxiang held the inner Censorate longest and possessed formidable authority.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingxiang held the inner Censorate longest and possessed formidable authority.

sentences.zh: 督團營，與郭勛共事，逡巡其間，不能有所振飭。

translations.literal: When he oversaw the regiment camps and worked alongside Guo Xun, he was circumspect in that partnership and could bring about no real reform.
translations.idiomatic: When he oversaw the regiment camps and worked alongside Guo Xun, he was circumspect in that partnership and could bring about no real reform.

sentences.zh: 給事中李鳳來等論權貴奪民利，章下都察院，廷相檄五城御史核實，遲四十余日。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries Li Fenglai and others discussed how the powerful seized the people's profit; the memorial was sent to the Censorate, and Tingxiang ordered the Five Cities censors to verify the facts, but they delayed more than forty days.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretaries Li Fenglai and others discussed how the powerful seized the people's profit; the memorial was sent to the Censorate, and Wang Tingxiang ordered the Five Cities censors to verify the facts, but they delayed more than forty days.

sentences.zh: 給事中章允賢遂劾廷相徇私慢上。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Zhang Yunxian thereupon impeached Tingxiang for favoritism and disrespect toward the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary Zhang Yunxian thereupon impeached Wang Tingxiang for favoritism and disrespect toward the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝方詰責，而廷相以御史所核聞，惟郭勛侵最多。

translations.literal: The emperor was just rebuking him when Tingxiang reported what the censors had verified, namely that Guo Xun alone had seized the most.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was just rebuking him when Wang Tingxiang reported what the censors had verified, namely that Guo Xun alone had seized the most.

sentences.zh: 帝令勛自奏，於是劾勛者群起。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Xun to memorialize in his own defense, and impeachments against Xun poured forth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Xun to memorialize in his own defense, and impeachments against Xun poured forth.

sentences.zh: 勛復以領敕稽留觸帝怒，下獄。

translations.literal: Xun again provoked the emperor's anger by delaying delivery of an imperial edict he had received, and was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Xun again provoked the emperor's anger by delaying delivery of an imperial edict he had received, and was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 責廷相朋比阿黨，斥為民。

translations.literal: Tingxiang was charged with factional collusion and expelled to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingxiang was charged with factional collusion and expelled to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 越三年卒。

translations.literal: Three years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he died.

sentences.zh: 廷相博學好議論，以經術稱。

translations.literal: Tingxiang was broadly learned and fond of debate, famed for his mastery of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingxiang was broadly learned and fond of debate, famed for his mastery of the classics.

sentences.zh: 於星歷、輿圖、樂律、河圖、洛書及周、邵、程、張之書，皆有所論駁，然其說頗乖僻。

translations.literal: On astronomy and calendrics, cartography, musical pitch, the River Diagram and Luo Writings, and the works of Zhou, Shao, Cheng, and Zhang, he had criticisms to offer in each case, yet his views were rather eccentric.
translations.idiomatic: On astronomy and calendrics, cartography, musical pitch, the River Diagram and Luo Writings, and the works of Zhou Dunyi, Shao Yong, the Cheng brothers, and Zhang Zai, he had criticisms to offer in each case, yet his views were rather eccentric.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，復官，贈少保，謚肅敏。

translations.literal: At the start of the Longqing reign his office was restored; he was posthumously given the rank of Junior Guardian and the posthumous title Summin.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Longqing reign his office was restored; he was posthumously given the rank of Junior Guardian and the posthumous title Summin.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：喬宇守南京，從容鎮靜，內嚴警備，可謂能當大事者矣。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Qiao Yu defended Nanjing with composure and calm, enforcing readiness within—he may be called a man equal to great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Qiao Yu defended Nanjing with composure and calm, enforcing readiness within—he may be called a man equal to great affairs.

sentences.zh: 觀宇與孫交等砥節奉公，懇懇廷諍，意在杜塞幸門，裨益國是。

translations.literal: Seeing how Yu, together with Sun Jiao and others, polished their integrity in public service and earnestly remonstrated at court, their intent was to block the gates of imperial favor and strengthen the national interest.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how Yu, together with Sun Jiao and others, polished their integrity in public service and earnestly remonstrated at court, their intent was to block the gates of imperial favor and strengthen the national interest.

sentences.zh: 雖得君行政，未能媲美蹇、夏，要其清嚴不茍，行無瑕尤，於前人亦不多讓。

translations.literal: Though they won the ruler's trust and governed, they could not match Jian and Xia; yet in their stern purity and unblemished conduct they yielded little to their predecessors.
translations.idiomatic: Though they won the ruler's trust and governed, they could not match Jian Shu and Xia Yuanji; yet in their stern purity and uncompromising integrity they yielded little to their predecessors.

sentences.zh: 蔣瑤為尚書，功名損於治郡，王廷相掌內臺，風力未著，是殆其時為之歟。

translations.literal: Jiang Yao as minister found his reputation diminished by his prefectural administration; Wang Tingxiang, presiding over the inner Censorate, never displayed firm authority—perhaps this was largely the fault of the times.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yao as minister found his reputation diminished by his prefectural administration; Wang Tingxiang, presiding over the inner Censorate, never displayed firm authority—perhaps this was largely the fault of the times.
